items.title: Deploy DUMB
items.text:
Choose the host or management tool where you want to install DUMB. Each link below opens the complete installation guide for that platform.

After installation, you will use the DUMB dashboard for everyday setup, service controls, updates and logs. The deployment guide covers the host setup needed to reach that dashboard.

Your environment Guide What it manages Linux terminal Docker Compose Compose file, storage, and container lifecycle Existing Portainer installation Portainer DUMB as a Portainer stack Existing Dockge installation Dockge DUMB as a Compose stack Unraid Unraid Community Applications template and host paths Windows WSL2 Docker Engine in a Linux distribution Proxmox Native LXC DUMB and managed services directly in a Debian guest Synology Container Manager A Compose project with NAS storage QNAP Container Station A Compose application with shared folders TrueNAS SCALE Custom App A Compose-based app with datasets

The native Proxmox helper has its own validation status and runtime requirements; read its guide before treating it as equivalent to the Docker image.

items.title: Choose an installation path
items.text:
Start with the host you already use. The platform links below provide the exact storage and installation steps.

flowchart TD
    Host["Where will DUMB run?"] --> Linux["Linux or a Docker host"]
    Host --> Windows["Windows: prepare WSL2 first"]
    Host --> NAS["NAS: use its Compose editor"]
    Host --> Proxmox["Proxmox: review native LXC validation"]
    Linux --> Terminal["Terminal: Docker Compose"]
    Linux --> Web["Web management: Portainer or Dockge"]
    Windows --> Linux
    NAS --> Editors["Synology, QNAP, TrueNAS or Unraid guide"]
    Terminal --> Dashboard["Open DUMB and complete onboarding"]
    Web --> Dashboard
    Editors --> Dashboard
    Proxmox --> Dashboard

items.title: Before starting
items.text:
Read Before you install for credentials, sizing, permissions, and persistence. Every normal deployment preserves these paths:

Path Purpose /config DUMB configuration and feature state /log DUMB and service logs /data Application data mapped through DUMB-managed internal paths /mnt/debrid Mounts and library paths

DUMB creates dumb_config.json when needed. Keep the host directories when replacing the container.

items.title: Choose the network and mount layout
items.text:
The default Compose file publishes port 3005 for the dashboard, REST gateway, and WebSockets. Embedded service UIs can use that same address. Publish individual service ports only when clients need direct access. See Networking and ports.

Use a normal /mnt/debrid bind if all consumers run inside DUMB. External consumers of FUSE/rclone submounts need a prepared shared Linux host mount and suitable propagation. See Before you install.

Windows hosts

Docker Desktop cannot provide the bind propagation required for external FUSE consumers. Use the WSL2 guide for Docker Engine on Windows.

items.title: After starting
items.text:
1. Open http://<host>:3005.
  2. Configure access and select services in Onboarding.
  3. Check service logs and finish application-specific setup.
  4. Test an import and playback through the applications you selected.

Keep a backup before changing persistent storage or moving hosts.

items.title: Deploy with Docker
items.text: Use Docker Compose to run DUMB on a Linux host. If you already manage containers with Portainer or Dockge, use that guide instead. Windows users should prepare WSL2 first.

items.title: From Compose to the dashboard
items.text:
Prepare the folders before starting the container. A running container is the start of application setup, rather than the final playback check.

flowchart TD
    Engine["Check Docker Engine and Compose"] --> Storage["Create config, log, data and media folders"]
    Storage --> Compose["Edit host paths, user IDs and published port"]
    Compose --> Validate["Validate the Compose file"]
    Validate --> Start["Start DUMB and follow startup logs"]
    Start --> Open["Open the dashboard on port 3005"]
    Open --> Setup["Complete onboarding and app setup"]
    Setup --> Test["Import and play one test item"]

items.title: 1. Check Docker Engine and Compose
items.text:
You need Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, a supported 64-bit host (amd64 or arm64), and a non-root account with permission to use Docker. Commands below use sudo for Docker operations.

Install Docker using its official package instructions for Ubuntu, Debian, or your distribution. Use a currently supported OS release. Docker's convenience script is intended for testing and development, so use the package repository for an ongoing installation.

docker --version
docker compose version
sudo docker run --rm hello-world

Avoid the Snap build for DUMB; its confinement can interfere with the mount and device access used by FUSE workflows. If you prefer Docker without sudo, follow Docker's Linux post-installation guide. Membership in the docker group grants control equivalent to host root.

items.title: 2. Prepare persistent storage
items.text:
Create a directory as the non-root account that will own DUMB's application data:

mkdir -p "$HOME/docker/DUMB"/{config,log,data,mnt/debrid}
cd "$HOME/docker/DUMB"
id -u
id -g

Keep the numeric UID and GID for the next step. PUID and PGID must be greater than zero.

Host subdirectory Path inside DUMB Contents config /config DUMB settings, authentication, and feature state log /log DUMB and collected application logs data /data Persistent application data mnt/debrid /mnt/debrid Mounts, generated links, and library paths

DUMB maps internal application paths such as /plex and /postgres_data into /data. Do not add a separate bind mount for every service on a new installation.

items.title: 3. Download and edit the Compose file
items.text:
curl --fail --show-error --location \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/I-am-PUID-0/DUMB/master/docker-compose.yml \
  --output docker-compose.yml

Open docker-compose.yml and review:

Setting What to enter Host volume paths Replace /home/username/docker/DUMB with the absolute directory created above PUID, PGID The nonzero values returned by id -u and id -g TZ A time zone such as Etc/UTC Image ghcr.io/i-am-puid-0/dumb:latest for the stable channel; see documentation versions for development Ports Keep 3005:3005 for normal dashboard/API access /dev/dri Keep for supported GPU acceleration; remove this device mapping if the host has no such device /dev/fuse, SYS_ADMIN, AppArmor option Required by workflows that create FUSE/rclone mounts

These guides use GitHub Container Registry (GHCR). Docker Hub remains available as iampuid0/dumb:<tag>. To move an existing deployment to GHCR, change the image reference and keep its tag, persistent mounts, and other settings. Pull the image with sudo docker compose pull, then recreate the container with sudo docker compose up -d.

For example, the environment section can use:

environment:
  - TZ=Etc/UTC
  - PUID=1000
  - PGID=1000

Use your actual user IDs. Do not leave the template's ID fields blank.

External consumers of FUSE mounts

A private /mnt/debrid bind is sufficient if all consumers run inside DUMB. If an external Arr or media-server container needs DUMB-created submounts, prepare a shared Linux host mount before adding :rshared. See Before you install. Docker Desktop does not support this propagation.

items.title: 4. Start DUMB
items.text:
From the directory containing the Compose file:

sudo docker compose config --quiet
sudo docker compose up -d
sudo docker compose logs --follow --tail=100

The first start may take longer while services are installed. Leave the process running and inspect the logs for the actual failure if startup stalls. Press Ctrl+C to leave the log viewer; this does not stop the detached container.

items.title: 5. Open the dashboard
items.text:
Open http://<host>:3005, then complete onboarding. The same listener forwards REST requests under /api and WebSockets under /ws.

The backend-native API binds to 127.0.0.1:8000 inside DUMB and is not published by the maintained Compose file.

If the page is unavailable, check:

sudo docker compose ps
sudo docker compose logs --tail=200

Confirm the published port, host firewall, and address. A service that starts successfully still needs its accounts, providers, root folders, and media libraries configured before an import/playback test.

items.title: Direct service access
items.text:
Embedded UIs can use the dashboard address. When another client needs a native service port, add it alongside 3005, using the assigned runtime port:

ports:
  - "3005:3005"
  - "7878:7878"   # Radarr, if its configured port is 7878
  - "32400:32400" # Plex

Apply changes with sudo docker compose up -d. Compare bridge and host networking in Networking and ports.

Do not publish 8000 for normal use. A mapping alone cannot expose its loopback listener; direct backend access also requires an intentional bind-address change and appropriate access controls.

items.title: Update or stop
items.text:
To adopt a new DUMB image while preserving bind-mounted data:

sudo docker compose pull
sudo docker compose up -d

DUMB's application auto-updates are separate from replacing the container image. Review Auto-update.

To stop without removing the container, use sudo docker compose stop. sudo docker compose down removes the container and Compose network while leaving the bind-mounted directories in place. Keep a backup before upgrades or storage changes.

For a shell when diagnosing a problem:

sudo docker compose exec DUMB bash

Use exit to leave the shell. If you attach to the container's main process instead, Docker's default detach sequence is Ctrl+P, then Ctrl+Q.

items.title: Deploy with Dockge
items.text: Dockge manages file-backed Docker Compose stacks. DUMB does not need a Dockge-specific image: use the maintained DUMB Compose file and replace its example host paths.

items.title: Create the Dockge stack
items.text:
Dockge manages the Compose stack; DUMB's dashboard manages the selected applications after the stack starts.

flowchart TD
    Storage["Prepare folders on the Docker host"] --> Stack["Dockge: create a new stack"]
    Stack --> Paste["Paste the maintained DUMB Compose file"]
    Paste --> Edit["Set host paths, TZ, PUID and PGID"]
    Edit --> Deploy["Deploy and read the stack terminal"]
    Deploy --> Dashboard["Open port 3005 and complete onboarding"]

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2
  • A working Dockge installation connected to the target Docker host
  • A numeric UID/GID with access to the persistent directories
  • /dev/fuse on the host if the selected workflow uses a FUSE or rclone mount

Dockge stores each stack as a normal compose.yaml. Its stacks directory must be mounted at the same path inside the Dockge container as on the host. See the Dockge installation and stacks documentation.

items.title: Prepare persistent storage
items.text:
Run this on the Docker host, not in the Dockge web terminal:

sudo install -d -o 1000 -g 1000 /opt/dumb
sudo install -d -o 1000 -g 1000 /opt/dumb/{config,log,data,mnt,mnt/debrid}

Replace 1000 with the nonzero UID and GID you will use for DUMB. These commands prepare new directories. For an existing installation, inspect its current ownership and mounts before changing them; do not recursively change the whole tree.

items.title: Create the stack
items.text:
1. In Dockge, choose Compose or New Stack.
  2. Name the stack dumb.
  3. Paste the current DUMB Compose file.
  4. Replace /home/username/docker/DUMB with /opt/dumb.
  5. Set TZ, PUID, and PGID.
  6. Deploy the stack and follow its terminal output.

The resulting storage and port section should resemble:

services:
  DUMB:
    image: ghcr.io/i-am-puid-0/dumb:latest
    container_name: DUMB
    volumes:
      - /opt/dumb/config:/config
      - /opt/dumb/log:/log
      - /opt/dumb/data:/data
      - /opt/dumb/mnt/debrid:/mnt/debrid
    environment:
      - TZ=UTC
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
    ports:
      - "3005:3005"

Keep the devices, cap_add, and security_opt entries from the maintained Compose file when the stack uses FUSE. Remove /dev/dri only when the host does not provide it and no selected service needs hardware acceleration.

items.title: External media-server mounts
items.text:
Prepare the producer host path as a shared Linux mount before relying on rshared/rslave. Compose propagation flags alone do not change the host mount. Check both the producer and consumer mount namespaces.

If Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, or an Arr runs in another container and must see a submount created inside DUMB, change the DUMB mount to:

- /opt/dumb/mnt/debrid:/mnt/debrid:rshared

Mount the same host path into each consumer at /mnt/debrid with rslave (or an equivalent propagation mode). This is unnecessary when all consumers run inside DUMB or the workflow exposes ordinary files/symlinks without a propagated submount.

items.title: Verify and update
items.text:
• Open http://<docker-host>:3005.
  • Check the Dockge stack terminal or DUMB container logs if startup fails.
  • Update by pulling the new image and redeploying the stack; do not delete the four persistent host directories.

Continue with Getting Started or review the configuration model.

items.title: Docker Networking and Ports
items.text:
Docker controls how applications inside the DUMB container become reachable from the Docker host and other devices. Choose one of the following Compose configurations.

Selected port publishing Host networking Compose setting ports: network_mode: host Exposed listeners Only listed ports All non-loopback listeners Host-to-container port translation Supported Not available Docker network isolation Retained Removed Best for Most installations Direct access to many service ports

WSL users

On WSL, the Docker host is the Linux distribution running inside WSL. Complete the WSL mirrored networking configuration before using the Windows machine's IPv4 address to access DUMB.

items.title: Option 1: Publish Selected Ports (Recommended)
items.text:
The maintained DUMB Compose file uses Docker's normal bridge networking and publishes only the DUMB Frontend:

services:
  DUMB:
    ports:
      - "3005:3005"

This shows the maintained bridge-mode example. The dashboard is the front door for API requests; publish additional service ports only when direct access is needed.

Open the dashboard at:

http://localhost:3005
http://<docker-host-ip>:3005

Add another mapping for each service that must be accessed directly. For example:

services:
  DUMB:
    ports:
      - "3005:3005" # DUMB Frontend and API gateway
      - "7878:7878" # Radarr
      - "8989:8989" # Sonarr
      - "32400:32400" # Plex

Use the Service ports reference and the actual port saved in DUMB when adding mappings. DUMB can move a service to the next available port when its preferred port is already in use.

This mode:

  • Keeps the container on an isolated Docker network
  • Exposes only the ports listed under ports:
  • Lets the host-side port differ from the container port, such as "17878:7878"
  • Requires updating and recreating the container when you add a direct service port

Embedded service UIs

If you use service UIs through the DUMB Frontend and its Traefik proxy, you may only need to publish 3005. Publish individual service ports when another device or application must connect to those services directly.

DUMB backend port 8000

Do not publish port 8000 for normal use. The DUMB Frontend proxies the API under http://<host>:3005/api, while the native backend listener binds to container loopback by default.

items.title: Option 2: Use Host Networking
items.text:
Host networking makes the DUMB container share the Docker host's network namespace. Services that listen on non-loopback addresses become reachable on the same port without adding a Compose mapping for each one.

Replace the entire ports: section with network_mode: host:

services:
  DUMB:
    network_mode: host

Do not keep ports: alongside network_mode: host. Port publishing is not used in host mode, and current Docker Compose versions reject that combination.

This mode:

  • Makes direct access to many DUMB-managed service ports more convenient
  • Avoids maintaining a long ports: list
  • Removes Docker's network isolation for the DUMB container
  • Prevents Docker from translating a conflicting host port to a different container port
  • Can expose more listeners than intended through the Docker host

Use host networking only when you want direct access to most service ports and are prepared to manage port conflicts and firewall rules. Keep DUMB authentication enabled. The native DUMB backend still binds to loopback; use the supported :3005/api gateway instead of relying on direct port 8000 access.

Platform support

These instructions target Docker Engine on Linux, including Docker Engine installed inside WSL. See Docker's host network driver documentation for platform-specific support and limitations.

items.title: Apply and Verify the Change
items.text:
After changing ports: or network_mode, recreate DUMB:

sudo docker compose down
sudo docker compose up -d

Then verify the effective network configuration:

sudo docker compose config
sudo docker ps

If a service is not reachable:

  • Confirm its current port in DUMB rather than assuming its default port
  • Check the Docker host's firewall
  • On WSL, check both Windows Firewall and the Hyper-V firewall
  • Confirm that ports: contains the current service port, or that host networking is active

For Compose syntax details, see Docker's network_mode and ports documentation.

items.title: Deploy with Portainer
items.text:
Use a Portainer stack to manage DUMB's Compose configuration. You need a running Docker environment in Portainer and permission to deploy a stack to it.

If Portainer is not installed, follow its official Docker installation guide. For Docker installation, use Docker Engine's supported packages. Avoid the Snap build for DUMB's FUSE workflows.

items.title: 1. Prepare paths on the Docker host
items.text:
Create persistent directories on the machine running Docker, not merely on the machine where your browser or Portainer server runs:

mkdir -p "$HOME/docker/DUMB"/{config,log,data,mnt/debrid}
id -u
id -g

Use the absolute path and nonzero IDs from the account that should own application data. Portainer stack files do not reliably expand ~.

items.title: 2. Prepare the Compose file
items.text:
Copy the maintained DUMB Compose file, or download it:

curl --fail --show-error --location \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/I-am-PUID-0/DUMB/master/docker-compose.yml \
  --output docker-compose.yml

Before deploying, edit:

  • The four host paths: replace /home/username/docker/DUMB with your absolute directory.
  • PUID and PGID: use nonzero IDs with access to those directories.
  • TZ: use your time zone, for example Etc/UTC.
  • Device mappings: keep /dev/fuse and its required capability/security options for FUSE workflows. Remove /dev/dri if the Docker host has no such device.
  • Image: use the stable latest image or the intended development image. Keep the docs channel aligned.

The standard file publishes 3005 for dashboard, API, WebSockets, and embedded UI access. A normal private /mnt/debrid bind works for consumers inside DUMB. See mount planning before enabling propagation for external consumers.

items.title: 3. Deploy the stack
items.text:
1. Open Portainer and select the intended Docker environment.
  2. Choose Stacks → Add stack.
  3. Enter dumb as the stack name.
  4. Choose Web editor and paste the reviewed Compose file.
  5. Select Deploy the stack.
Portainer screens

Labels may differ by Portainer version.

items.title: 4. Verify startup
items.text:
Open Containers, select DUMB, then open Logs. Follow startup and check any reported installation or permissions error.

Open http://<docker-host>:3005 and complete onboarding. Check that the host address belongs to the selected Docker environment; a remote agent's containers do not run on the Portainer server by default.

For a diagnostic shell, use the container's Console action and select /bin/bash or /bin/sh. This is separate from attaching to the container's existing main process.

items.title: Direct application ports
items.text:
Add mappings only when another client needs direct access, for example:

ports:
  - "3005:3005"
  - "7878:7878" # Radarr, if its actual assigned port is 7878

Update the stack after changing mappings. See Service ports and Networking.

The DUMB backend on 8000 is loopback-only by default. Prefer the gateway at :3005/api/...; a Portainer port mapping alone does not expose the backend listener.

items.title: Update the DUMB image
items.text:
1. Open Stacks → dumb → Editor.
  2. Review Compose changes against your existing paths and settings. Preserve your values rather than replacing the file blindly.
  3. Select Update the stack and choose the option to re-pull the image when offered.
  4. Check the container logs and dashboard after replacement.

Application auto-updates inside DUMB do not update the DUMB image itself. Keep /config, /data, /log, and library mounts across replacement, and keep a separate backup before upgrades.

items.title: Deploying DUMB on Proxmox
items.text:
The native helper runs DUMB and its managed services directly in one LXC, without a Docker layer. The helper currently uses the maintainer validation branch described below.

This keeps the normal DUMB topology simple:

Proxmox host
└── DUMB LXC
    ├── DUMB API and frontend
    ├── rclone / Decypharr / InfiniDysk
    ├── Arr applications
    └── Plex / Jellyfin / Emby

Because every consumer is in the same LXC, DUMB-created FUSE mounts only need to exist inside that LXC. No mount propagation back to the Proxmox host is required.

items.title: Native LXC installation boundaries
items.text:
The native helper keeps DUMB and its managed applications in one LXC. Applications in another LXC need an explicit storage-sharing plan.

flowchart TD
    Host["Proxmox host: run the reviewed helper"] --> LXC["Dedicated DUMB LXC"]
    LXC --> Controller["DUMB controller and dashboard"]
    Controller --> Apps["Managed workflow apps and media servers"]
    Controller --> Storage["Persistent config, data and media paths"]
    Browser["Your browser"] --> Dashboard["LXC address on port 3005"]
    Dashboard --> Controller
    External["Apps in another LXC"] -. "Separate sharing plan required" .-> Storage

items.title: Install the validation build
items.text:
While the helper is awaiting upstream acceptance, run the maintainer-fork build from the Proxmox VE host shell:

COMMUNITY_SCRIPTS_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/I-am-PUID-0/ProxmoxVED/feat/dumb" \
  bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/I-am-PUID-0/ProxmoxVED/feat/dumb/ct/dumb.sh)"

COMMUNITY_SCRIPTS_URL makes the shared Community Scripts engine fetch the matching install/dumb-install.sh from the same fork and branch. Do not omit it while using the validation build.

The default controller source is the latest stable DUMB release. For an advanced test installation, set DUMB Controller Branch in the script generator's app settings or pass var_dumb_branch from the host shell. For example, this installs the current dev branch:

var_dumb_branch=dev \
COMMUNITY_SCRIPTS_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/I-am-PUID-0/ProxmoxVED/feat/dumb" \
  bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/I-am-PUID-0/ProxmoxVED/feat/dumb/ct/dumb.sh)"

Any valid branch in I-am-PUID-0/DUMB can be selected. Branch heads are mutable development targets and may be less stable than a published release; the same candidate validation and controller rollback protections still apply. Take an independent backup first: controller rollback restores /opt/dumb, but it does not reverse configuration migrations or application-state changes under /config or /data.

Validation build

This branch is for controlled testing before the upstream pull request. Use a new LXC, keep independent backups, and report the DUMB version plus the relevant journalctl -u dumb output when a test fails.

After the script is validated, submitted to community-scripts/ProxmoxVED, and promoted into community-scripts/ProxmoxVE, the production command will become:

bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/community-scripts/ProxmoxVE/main/ct/dumb.sh)"

The default installation creates an unprivileged Debian 13 LXC with:

  • 4 vCPU;
  • 8 GiB RAM;
  • 40 GiB disk;
  • FUSE enabled for rclone and other DUMB-managed mounts;
  • optional Intel/AMD GPU device passthrough; and
  • DUMB plus its required runtimes installed directly on the guest OS.

Use Advanced Settings when a large stack, source builds, the install cache, or a media server needs more resources. Both amd64 and arm64 have completed the recorded native acceptance tests with DUMB 2.21.0: clean Proxmox VE installation, controller update and rollback, reboot, FUSE namespace isolation, and stopped backup/restore. That qualification applies to the tested versions; it does not establish every later application update or GPU path.

When installation finishes, open:

http://<DUMB-LXC-IP>:3005

The frontend can take several minutes to appear on first boot while DUMB installs its initial managed services. Follow progress inside the LXC with:

journalctl -u dumb -f

Then continue with Getting Started.

items.title: .NET repository checks
items.text:
Debian 13 has an official Microsoft .NET feed. An updater message claiming that the feed does not exist can also come from a failed network probe.

The DUMB install/update scripts wrap the existing Community Scripts .NET installer with a local repository check. On Debian, this check runs before the shared installer can remove an existing Microsoft source/keyring, retries transient failures, and reuses a successful result for the duration of that .NET setup invocation. Failed checks stop the update before repository changes. The wrapper also avoids the shared probe's reversed cached success/failure handling without modifying core or changing checks for other applications.

Use the updated DUMB helper scripts for this fix; updating only DUMB's Python controller does not change native runtime reconciliation. No core fork or COMMUNITY_SCRIPTS_CORE_URL override is required. Existing running services remain on the previous controller if dependency reconciliation fails before activation.

items.title: Native LXC paths
items.text:
LXC path Purpose /opt/dumb DUMB controller source and Python environment /config DUMB configuration, authentication state, snapshots, and feature state /data Persistent managed-service data /log DUMB and managed-service logs /mnt/debrid FUSE mounts, generated links, and symlink libraries /postgres_data DUMB-managed PostgreSQL cluster when enabled /zurg/config.yml, /zurg/plex_update.sh Base Zurg files copied into newly configured Zurg instances /etc/dumb/controller-source Root-managed stable or branch selection used by update /etc/systemd/system/dumb.service Native DUMB systemd service

These are normal LXC filesystem paths, not Docker bind mounts. DUMB preserves its established internal paths so the same service configuration works in the native and container-image deployments.

The helper also configures systemd-logind to retain IPC owned by DUMB's managed-service UID. This is required for PostgreSQL POSIX shared memory after temporary setup sessions end. Package-provided PostgreSQL, Plex, and Jellyfin systemd units are kept inactive because DUMB, not the distribution unit, supervises those processes inside this dedicated LXC.

items.title: GPU passthrough and Jellyfin
items.text:
When GPU passthrough is enabled, the installer invokes the Community Scripts hardware-acceleration helper to select the vendor's drivers and required Debian repository components. The update path also reconciles drivers when updating the controller. Intel GPU support requires the appropriate VA-API driver; OpenCL tone mapping additionally depends on a compute runtime compatible with the GPU generation. Installing a package does not prove either path works.

DUMB creates and maintains its own service account. Adding only the package-created jellyfin account to render/video does not grant access to DUMB's Jellyfin process. After applying the installer and controller fixes, restart DUMB and inspect the actual Jellyfin process:

pgrep -a -f '/usr/lib/jellyfin/bin/jellyfin'
ls -ln /dev/dri/renderD*
# Replace <PID> with the Jellyfin PID shown above.
grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|Groups):' /proc/<PID>/status

The command should select /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffmpeg unless a custom path was configured. The process's primary or supplementary groups must include the render device's numeric GID. For an unprivileged LXC, unmapped ownership must be corrected in the Proxmox device mapping; making render nodes world-writable is not required by DUMB.

Verify playback by forcing a transcode and checking the Jellyfin FFmpeg log for the selected binary, QSV/VA-API codec, and successful device initialization. Testing only as root can conceal service-user permission failures. See the Jellyfin service guide.

items.title: Manage and update DUMB
items.text:
Useful commands inside the LXC:

systemctl status dumb
journalctl -u dumb -f
systemctl restart dumb

Run the Community Scripts updater inside the LXC to update the currently selected DUMB source. Stable installations follow the latest published release, while branch installations follow the current head of their saved branch:

update

To switch an existing LXC to dev or another DUMB branch, pass the branch for one update run:

DUMB_CONTROLLER_BRANCH=dev update

The branch choice is saved only after the candidate starts and passes the API health check, so later update runs continue following it. Return to the stable release channel with:

DUMB_CONTROLLER_BRANCH=latest update

Switching back to stable can be a controller downgrade. Verify that the branch did not introduce configuration or data changes that the stable release cannot read before making that switch.

The updater reconciles the required native dependencies, downloads the new controller into a candidate directory, builds its locked Python environment, and validates it while the current controller is still running. It then backs up /opt/dumb, stops DUMB only for activation, starts the candidate, and waits for the API health check. A failed build, start, or health check automatically restores and verifies the previous controller. An interrupted update is recovered the next time update runs.

Configuration and managed application data under /config, /data, /postgres_data, and /mnt/debrid remain outside the replaced controller directory. The update backup is removed after the replacement passes health verification.

Use DUMB's own Updates controls for the individual services it manages.

items.title: Backups and FUSE
items.text:
Back up at least /config and /data, plus any application-native backups required by the services you enabled. /mnt/debrid normally contains live or re-creatable mount views and should not be treated as the only copy of data.

Proxmox snapshot backups and FUSE

Proxmox strongly advises against FUSE mounts inside an LXC because freezing the container for suspend/snapshot-mode backups can fail. Prefer a stopped-mode backup window after stopping DUMB, or otherwise test the exact backup mode and mount stack before relying on it.

items.title: Existing Plex or Arr applications in other LXCs
items.text:
An external Plex or Arr LXC cannot see /mnt/debrid merely because it uses the same path name. It needs a separately designed storage boundary that exposes both the symlink library and every target path those symlinks reference.

The helper deliberately does not add that boundary automatically. Reverse propagation of a mount created inside an LXC depends on the host mount namespace, LXC propagation flags, FUSE permissions, UID/GID mappings, backup behavior, and the consumer's own mount namespace. A configuration that gets one of those boundaries wrong can look healthy until a remount leaves Plex or an Arr app on a stale path.

Choose one of these approaches:

  1. Move the consumer into the DUMB LXC. This is the supported and simplest layout.
  2. Mount the remote storage on the Proxmox host, then bind-mount the same host-managed tree into DUMB and every consumer LXC. In that layout, disable the duplicate DUMB-managed rclone mount and keep the same absolute paths in all applications.
  3. Export the complete DUMB mount/link tree through a deliberately managed network filesystem and mount it in each consumer. Validate symlink target paths, permissions, disconnect/reconnect behavior, and startup ordering.
  4. Build a custom rshared/rslave LXC topology only after proving mount and unmount propagation in both directions on the exact Proxmox/LXC version.

Do not add a host mount over an active /mnt/debrid

A new bind mount hides the directory that was previously at that path. If DUMB is already configured, stop it, take independent backups, and migrate the mount and symlink trees deliberately. Never attach an empty host path over an active deployment and assume the old files moved into it.

For a custom propagation topology, verify all of the following before allowing an Arr import or media-server scan:

# DUMB LXC
findmnt -R /mnt/debrid
findmnt -no TARGET,PROPAGATION /mnt/debrid

# Proxmox host and every consumer LXC
findmnt -R <shared-path>
readlink <representative-symlink>

Test a provider remount while each consumer is running. A consumer should see the replacement mount without retaining Transport endpoint is not connected. Also confirm that consumer unmounts cannot propagate back and tear down DUMB's producer mount.

items.title: The DUMB page is unavailable
items.text:
Inside the LXC:

systemctl status dumb --no-pager
journalctl -u dumb -n 200 --no-pager
ss -lntp | grep -E ':(8000|3005)\b'

The API normally listens on port 8000; the user-facing frontend is port 3005. The LXC firewall and network must allow the frontend port from your operator workstation.

items.title: /dev/fuse is missing
items.text:
On the Proxmox host, inspect the generated container configuration:

pct config <CTID> | grep -E 'features|dev/fuse'

The Community Scripts default enables FUSE. Stop and start the LXC after fixing its configuration; restarting only the DUMB service cannot add a missing device to the LXC.

items.title: A managed service cannot find a runtime
items.text:
Confirm the native toolchain and controller environment:

python3.11 --version
python3.12 --version
node --version
pnpm --version
go version
dotnet --info
rclone version
/opt/dumb/venv/bin/python -m pip check

Run update to repair the DUMB controller source/environment. Service-specific install failures remain visible in journalctl -u dumb and can then be retried from the DUMB UI.

items.title: PostgreSQL reports a missing shared-memory segment
items.text:
If several PostgreSQL-backed services fail together and the journal contains could not open shared memory segment "/PostgreSQL...", verify the native LXC safeguard:

systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/logind.conf | grep -A2 dumb.conf

The effective configuration must include RemoveIPC=no. Run update, then restart DUMB, if the drop-in is absent. A healthy restart recreates the PostgreSQL shared-memory objects and keeps them after the managed UID's setup session closes.

items.title: Plex fails to install or cannot create its Cache directory
items.text:
Older test builds created a direct /etc/systemd/system/plexmediaserver.service mask before Plex was installed. Plex's Debian package rejects that path during its pre-install check. If the package was then repaired manually, the generated /plex/Plex Media Server tree could also remain owned by the package account.

Current LXC helpers use a supported systemd drop-in with an unmet condition. That lets the Debian package install successfully without starting its own Plex process; DUMB remains the only process supervisor and repairs the writable tree.

test ! -e /etc/systemd/system/plexmediaserver.service
systemctl cat plexmediaserver.service | grep -F 'ConditionPathExists=/run/dumb-allow-package-services'
systemctl is-active plexmediaserver.service

The first command should produce no output, the second should show the condition, and the package-owned unit should report inactive. For an LXC created with an older test build, reconcile the helper and restart the DUMB controller:

update
systemctl restart dumb

If dpkg still reports an interrupted installation, complete its pending work after update has removed the legacy mask:

dpkg --configure -a
apt-get -f install

items.title: Deploy with QNAP Container Station
items.text: QNAP Container Station can create a Docker Compose application from YAML. The labels can vary slightly by Container Station/QTS version, but the official flow is Create → Create Application → paste and validate the Compose YAML.

items.title: Create the QNAP application
items.text:
Container Station creates the application from Compose. Review the host paths and permissions before starting it.

flowchart TD
    Share["Prepare persistent shared folders"] --> Create["Container Station: Create Application"]
    Create --> YAML["Paste the maintained Compose YAML"]
    YAML --> Settings["Replace share paths and set user IDs"]
    Settings --> Validate["Validate YAML and create the application"]
    Validate --> Dashboard["Open the QNAP address on port 3005"]

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• A QNAP model/architecture supported by the DUMB image (amd64 or arm64)
  • Container Station installed and current
  • Shared folders for persistent DUMB data
  • A QNAP user UID/GID with read/write access to those folders
  • FUSE device/capability support if the selected workflow creates FUSE mounts

See QNAP's Creating an Application instructions for the Compose application workflow.

items.title: Prepare the shared folders
items.text:
Create a DUMB directory under a persistent share, with these subdirectories:

/share/Container/DUMB/
├── config/
├── data/
├── log/
└── mnt/debrid/

Your QNAP share name can differ. Use its absolute host path in the Compose file and grant the selected PUID:PGID ownership or read/write access.

items.title: Create the application
items.text:
1. Download or copy the current DUMB Compose file.
  2. In Container Station, open Create → Create Application.
  3. Name the application dumb and paste the YAML.
  4. Replace /home/username/docker/DUMB with /share/Container/DUMB (or your actual share path).
  5. Set TZ, PUID, and PGID.
  6. Validate the YAML and create the application.

The persistent mounts should be:

volumes:
  - /share/Container/DUMB/config:/config
  - /share/Container/DUMB/log:/log
  - /share/Container/DUMB/data:/data
  - /share/Container/DUMB/mnt/debrid:/mnt/debrid

The maintained Compose file publishes the DUMB frontend on 3005. Open http://<qnap-address>:3005 after the application becomes healthy.

items.title: FUSE and external consumers
items.text:
Prepare the producer host path as a shared Linux mount before relying on rshared/rslave. Compose propagation flags alone do not change the host mount. Check both the producer and consumer mount namespaces.

The maintained Compose file requests /dev/fuse, SYS_ADMIN, and an unconfined AppArmor profile. Keep those entries for workflows that mount with rclone/FUSE. Availability depends on the QNAP kernel and Container Station version; if the application rejects them, check the QNAP host before removing the settings.

When another container must see a DUMB-created submount, use :rshared on the DUMB /mnt/debrid bind and :rslave on the consumer bind. If Container Station cannot preserve those propagation modes, use an all-in-one DUMB workflow or a workflow based on ordinary files/symlinks instead of assuming external FUSE mounts will propagate.

items.title: Update and recover
items.text:
• Pull ghcr.io/i-am-puid-0/dumb:latest, then recreate/redeploy the application.
  • Preserve /share/Container/DUMB/config, data, log, and mnt/debrid.
  • Use Container Station logs first; then review Troubleshooting and Service ports.

Do not publish backend port 8000 for normal use. The frontend proxies the API under http://<qnap-address>:3005/api.

items.title: Deploy with Synology Container Manager
items.text: DSM 7.2 Container Manager supports Docker Compose through Projects. A project can upload a Compose file or use the built-in YAML editor.

items.title: Create the Synology project
items.text:
Use the persistent shared folder in the Compose mappings so a project update keeps DUMB's settings and application data.

flowchart TD
    Folders["Create the DUMB folders in a persistent share"] --> Permissions["Grant access to the chosen UID and GID"]
    Permissions --> Project["Container Manager: Project → Create"]
    Project --> Compose["Upload or paste Compose and replace host paths"]
    Compose --> Start["Create and start the project"]
    Start --> Dashboard["Open the NAS address on port 3005"]

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• A Synology model/architecture supported by the DUMB image (amd64 or arm64)
  • DSM Container Manager installed
  • A shared folder for persistent DUMB storage
  • A numeric UID/GID with read/write access to that folder
  • /dev/fuse and the required container capabilities if the selected workflow creates FUSE mounts

Synology documents the project workflow in Container Manager: Project.

items.title: Prepare persistent storage
items.text:
Create this structure in File Station or over SSH:

/volume1/docker/DUMB/
├── config/
├── data/
├── log/
└── mnt/debrid/

Replace volume1 if the share is on another volume. Apply permissions for the same UID/GID you will enter as PUID and PGID.

items.title: Create the project
items.text:
1. Open Container Manager → Project → Create.
  2. Enter a project name such as dumb and choose a project working directory.
  3. Upload or paste the current DUMB Compose file.
  4. Replace /home/username/docker/DUMB with /volume1/docker/DUMB.
  5. Set TZ, PUID, and PGID.
  6. Review the summary, create the project, and start it.

The persistent mounts should resolve to:

volumes:
  - /volume1/docker/DUMB/config:/config
  - /volume1/docker/DUMB/log:/log
  - /volume1/docker/DUMB/data:/data
  - /volume1/docker/DUMB/mnt/debrid:/mnt/debrid

Open http://<synology-address>:3005. DUMB API requests use the frontend proxy at /api; the native backend on 8000 is intentionally not published.

items.title: FUSE and mount propagation
items.text:
Prepare the producer host path as a shared Linux mount before relying on rshared/rslave. Compose propagation flags alone do not change the host mount. Check both the producer and consumer mount namespaces.

Keep /dev/fuse, SYS_ADMIN, and the security options from the maintained Compose file when your workflow needs rclone/FUSE. Support can vary by DSM, model, and kernel. A successful container start alone does not prove that an external media-server container can see nested mounts.

For external consumers, set the DUMB bind to:

- /volume1/docker/DUMB/mnt/debrid:/mnt/debrid:rshared

Mount that host directory into the consumer at /mnt/debrid using rslave or an equivalent propagation mode. If DSM does not preserve propagation, keep the producer and consumers inside DUMB or select a workflow that exposes ordinary files/symlinks.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
In Project, edit the YAML if the upstream Compose file changed, pull the current image, and rebuild/recreate the project. Do not use Clean or delete the persistent shared folders unless you intend to remove DUMB data.

Continue with Getting Started.

items.title: Deploy with TrueNAS SCALE
items.text: TrueNAS SCALE 24.10 and later use Docker for Apps and can deploy a custom application from Docker Compose YAML. Older 24.04 and earlier releases use the archived Kubernetes app model and are not covered by this Compose procedure.

items.title: From datasets to the DUMB app
items.text:
The dataset holds persistent state. Installing or updating the custom app should continue using that same dataset.

flowchart TD
    Dataset["Create a DUMB dataset and subdirectories"] --> ACL["Set dataset access for the chosen UID and GID"]
    ACL --> Apps["Apps → Discover Apps → Install via YAML"]
    Apps --> Compose["Paste Compose and replace dataset paths"]
    Compose --> Save["Save the custom app and inspect startup"]
    Save --> Dashboard["Open port 3005 and complete onboarding"]

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• TrueNAS SCALE 24.10 or later with an Apps pool selected
  • Datasets/directories for DUMB's persistent storage
  • Dataset ACLs that permit the selected PUID:PGID to read and write
  • FUSE device/capability support if the selected workflow uses rclone/FUSE

TrueNAS documents the current editor under Install Custom App via YAML.

items.title: Create datasets and directories
items.text:
Create a dedicated dataset such as tank/apps/dumb, then create:

/mnt/tank/apps/dumb/
├── config/
├── data/
├── log/
└── mnt/debrid/

Use your actual pool/dataset name. Host-path datasets are easier to back up and inspect than hidden app-managed volumes. Set ACLs/ownership for the UID/GID DUMB will run as; the TrueNAS apps user's default IDs are not automatically the right IDs for DUMB.

items.title: Install via YAML
items.text:
1. Open Apps → Discover Apps.
  2. Use the menu beside Custom App and choose Install via YAML.
  3. Name the app dumb.
  4. Paste the current DUMB Compose file.
  5. Replace /home/username/docker/DUMB with /mnt/tank/apps/dumb.
  6. Set TZ, PUID, and PGID, then save the app.

The storage section should resemble:

volumes:
  - /mnt/tank/apps/dumb/config:/config
  - /mnt/tank/apps/dumb/log:/log
  - /mnt/tank/apps/dumb/data:/data
  - /mnt/tank/apps/dumb/mnt/debrid:/mnt/debrid

Open http://<truenas-address>:3005 after the workload starts. The frontend proxies DUMB's API under /api; do not expose native backend port 8000 unless you deliberately change its bind address, enable authentication, and restrict network access.

items.title: FUSE and external media servers
items.text:
Prepare the producer host path as a shared Linux mount before relying on rshared/rslave. Compose propagation flags alone do not change the host mount. Check both the producer and consumer mount namespaces.

The maintained Compose file includes /dev/fuse, SYS_ADMIN, and an unconfined AppArmor profile. Keep them for mount-producing workflows. Remove /dev/dri only if that device is absent and no configured service needs it.

If another TrueNAS App must see submounts created by DUMB, use :rshared on DUMB's /mnt/debrid host bind and a compatible slave propagation mode in the consumer. TrueNAS performs only basic YAML validation, so verify the effective container mounts after deployment rather than assuming the UI accepted every Compose option.

items.title: Updates and backups
items.text:
• Edit/redeploy the custom app to adopt Compose changes and pull a new image.
  • Back up config and service data under data; preserve the chosen workflow's library/link state under mnt/debrid where applicable.
  • Dataset snapshots are useful, but database-aware logical backups are still required for PostgreSQL portability. See PostgreSQL FAQ.

Continue with Getting Started.

items.title: Deploy DUMB on Unraid
items.text: Deploy DUMB from the Community Applications template when it is available, or add it as a Compose stack/container using the maintained settings below. The same persistence and path rules apply to both methods.

items.title: Install and check the Unraid container
items.text:
The application template sets up the container. The first import and playback check happens after DUMB and the selected apps have been configured.

flowchart TD
    Apps["Apps: find the DUMB template"] --> Review["Review image, persistent paths and user IDs"]
    Review --> Apply["Apply the template"]
    Apply --> Logs["Follow the container log through startup"]
    Logs --> Dashboard["Open DUMB on port 3005"]
    Dashboard --> Setup["Complete onboarding and app setup"]
    Setup --> Test["Test import and playback"]

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Unraid with Docker enabled
  • Community Applications for the template-based path
  • A persistent appdata directory and sufficient space for selected services
  • A UID/GID that owns the mapped directories
  • /dev/fuse access for workflows that create rclone/FUSE mounts

items.title: Install from Community Applications
items.text:
1. Open Apps, search for DUMB, and select the Distributed Unlimited Media Bridge template.
  2. Set the image to ghcr.io/i-am-puid-0/dumb:latest (or the release tag you intend to run).
  3. Configure the four persistent mappings shown below.
  4. Set TZ, PUID, and PGID to values that can access those shares.
  5. Keep /dev/fuse, SYS_ADMIN, and the required security settings when your workflow uses FUSE.
  6. Apply the template and follow the container log through first startup.

The common Unraid nobody:users identity is 99:100, but do not copy those values blindly. Use the owner of your appdata/media paths, and correct existing directory permissions before starting DUMB.

items.title: Persistent path mappings
items.text:
Use a layout such as:

Unraid host path Container path Purpose /mnt/user/appdata/DUMB/config /config Runtime configuration, auth, metrics, jobs /mnt/user/appdata/DUMB/log /log DUMB and managed-service logs /mnt/user/appdata/DUMB/data /data Service-specific persistent application data /mnt/user/appdata/DUMB/mnt/debrid /mnt/debrid Mounts, links, and library trees

Do not replace the /data mapping with a generic /mnt mapping. DUMB maps internal paths such as /plex, /altmount, and /postgres_data into the persistent /data tree.

If you deploy through Compose, start from the current DUMB Compose file and replace /home/username/docker/DUMB with /mnt/user/appdata/DUMB.

items.title: Open DUMB
items.text:
The maintained deployment publishes the frontend at:

http://<unraid-address>:3005

The frontend proxies DUMB API calls under /api. The backend-native 8000 listener remains private by default; do not publish it for ordinary use.

items.title: Share library paths with another container
items.text:
Use the same container-visible path in DUMB and the external Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Sonarr, Radarr, or other consumer:

/mnt/debrid

Then select the curated library produced by your workflow, for example:

  • /mnt/debrid/riven_symlinks
  • /mnt/debrid/clid_symlinks
  • /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks
  • /mnt/debrid/infinidysk-symlinks
  • /mnt/debrid/combined_symlinks
  • the AltMount import directory configured for that instance

Do not point a media library at an entire raw provider mount unless that is explicitly the workflow you designed.

items.title: Mount propagation
items.text:
Prepare the producer host path as a shared Linux mount before relying on rshared/rslave. Compose propagation flags alone do not change the host mount. Check both the producer and consumer mount namespaces.

When DUMB creates a nested FUSE/rclone mount that another container must see:

  • DUMB's host bind must be rshared.
  • Consumer containers should mount the same host path with rslave (or an equivalent slave propagation mode).
  • Restart consumers after changing propagation settings and verify the nested mount from inside each container.

Propagation is unnecessary for ordinary symlink/file trees and when every consumer runs inside DUMB.

items.title: Permissions
items.text:
Check the selected IDs and the exact directory before changing ownership:

id <user>
ls -ld /mnt/user/appdata/DUMB /mnt/user/appdata/DUMB/{config,data,log}

DUMB's controller prepares service ownership at startup. Do not recursively chown the entire DUMB tree: private controller state under /config can intentionally have a different owner from managed applications, and a nested media mount can expose a much larger tree than expected. Fix only the specific incorrect host directory after stopping its writers and checking its mounts.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
View the container log from the Docker tab, or inspect from an Unraid terminal:

docker logs -f DUMB
docker exec -it DUMB bash
docker exec DUMB findmnt -R /mnt/debrid

Do not install ad-hoc tools into the running container; those changes disappear on recreation and can alter the supported runtime. Useful checks are already available through the DUMB UI, logs, and standard Ubuntu utilities in the image.

Common causes of failure are:

  • incorrect appdata ownership or mismatched PUID/PGID
  • missing /dev/fuse or SYS_ADMIN for a FUSE workflow
  • inconsistent paths between DUMB and external consumers
  • missing rshared/rslave propagation for nested mounts
  • a host port already in use

Continue with Getting Started, then review Service ports before publishing any additional UI.

items.title: Deploy with WSL2
items.text:
Run Docker Engine inside a WSL2 Linux distribution. This gives DUMB the Linux mount behavior needed by FUSE/rclone workflows. Docker Desktop does not support sharing these submounts through bind propagation.

Avoid running both Docker Desktop integration and a separate Docker Engine against the same distribution without an explicit plan. Check which Docker daemon your CLI targets before deploying.

items.title: Windows and Linux responsibilities
items.text:
Run the Docker commands and keep application data inside WSL's Linux filesystem. Windows reaches the published dashboard through the configured WSL network.

flowchart TD
    Windows["Windows: install or update WSL"] --> Linux["WSL2 Linux distribution"]
    Linux --> Docker["Install Docker Engine inside Linux"]
    Linux --> Storage["Keep config and databases in Linux storage"]
    Docker --> DUMB["Deploy DUMB with Compose or Portainer"]
    Storage --> DUMB
    DUMB --> Browser["Windows browser: try localhost:3005"]
    Browser --> LAN["For LAN access: review WSL networking and firewall"]

items.title: 1. Install or update WSL
items.text:
In PowerShell as administrator, install WSL if needed:

wsl --install

Restart Windows if prompted, open the installed Linux distribution, and create a non-root Linux user. For an existing WSL installation:

wsl --update
wsl --list --verbose

The chosen distribution must show version 2. To select or convert a distribution, use its exact name from the list:

wsl --set-default <DistroName>
wsl --set-version <DistroName> 2

See Microsoft's WSL installation guide for supported Windows versions and installation troubleshooting. Choose a distribution supported by Docker Engine rather than an old version solely to match a screenshot.

items.title: 2. Install Docker Engine in Linux
items.text:
Inside WSL, follow Docker's Ubuntu or Debian package instructions. Check that systemd and Docker are available:

ps -p 1 -o comm=
sudo systemctl status docker
docker compose version

If the distribution does not use systemd, follow Microsoft's systemd instructions. WSL and Docker must be running for DUMB to remain available; plan startup after Windows restarts separately.

Keep DUMB's configuration and databases in the Linux filesystem, for example $HOME/docker/DUMB, rather than a Windows-mounted directory under /mnt/c.

items.title: 3. Deploy DUMB
items.text:
Choose one path:

  • Docker Compose for terminal management.
  • Portainer for a web interface.

Deploy once using the chosen method. The Docker host in those guides is the WSL Linux distribution.

Try http://localhost:3005 from Windows after startup. If you need LAN access or access through the Windows host's IPv4 address, review mirrored networking below and the Windows/Hyper-V firewall rules.

items.title: Mirrored mode networking
items.text:
On supported Windows 11 versions, WSL can mirror Windows network interfaces. See Microsoft's WSL networking documentation for current requirements and limitations.

Open %UserProfile%\.wslconfig from PowerShell:

notepad $env:USERPROFILE\.wslconfig

Merge these settings into the existing file:

[wsl2]
networkingMode=mirrored

[experimental]
hostAddressLoopback=true

hostAddressLoopback allows Windows and WSL to reach each other through IPv4 addresses assigned to the Windows host, in addition to loopback. It only applies in mirrored mode. Optional autoProxy=true belongs under [wsl2] when Windows proxy propagation is needed.

Apply the changes when it is safe to stop all WSL distributions:

wsl --shutdown
wsl

Windows Firewall and the Hyper-V firewall can still block inbound connections. Allow the intended DUMB listener on trusted networks rather than assuming mirrored mode publishes every service. See WSL advanced settings.

items.title: External consumers of FUSE mounts
items.text:
All-in-one workflows do not need propagation to the WSL host. External Linux containers reading DUMB-created submounts need a shared host mount and matching bind propagation. Prepare only the intended host mount rather than changing the entire filesystem's propagation without review.

The propagation state must be restored after WSL restarts. See the rclone mount-propagation guide, and verify the nested mount from the consumer container before relying on playback.

Windows Explorer access to \\wsl.localhost\<DistroName>\... is a separate sharing path. It does not establish that a Windows media server can follow Linux symlinks or use every FUSE mount correctly. Test the exact consumer.

To browse a Linux directory in Explorer:

explorer.exe .

Use Networking and ports when choosing Docker bridge mappings or host networking.

items.title: Authentication FAQ
items.text: Common questions and troubleshooting for DUMB's authentication system.

items.title: Choose the right login recovery path
items.text:
A rejected password, an expired session and a complete lockout have different recovery paths. Use another active account where one is available before considering the manual reset procedure.

flowchart TD
    Issue["What happens when you sign in?"] --> Password["Invalid credentials"]
    Issue --> Disabled["Account is disabled"]
    Issue --> Session["A previous session expired"]
    Issue --> Lockout["No usable account remains"]
    Password --> Check["Check username, password and case"]
    Disabled --> Active["Ask an active account holder to review the user"]
    Session --> Login["Sign in again and check system time if expiry repeats"]
    Lockout --> Recovery["Follow the documented lockout recovery procedure"]

items.title: Do I need to enable authentication?
items.text: Enable authentication whenever other people or networks can reach DUMB. Every enabled account currently has operator permissions; an extra account is not a read-only role. Only leave authentication disabled in an intentionally trusted, isolated environment.

items.title: How do I create the first user account?
items.text:
When DUMB starts with no users:

  1. Navigate to the DUMB frontend
  2. You'll be redirected to /setup
  3. Enter a username and password
  4. Click Create Account

items.title: Can I change my password?
items.text:
Currently, password changes require:

  1. Creating a temporary second user
  2. Signing in as the temporary user
  3. Deleting the original user (users cannot delete their own current account)
  4. Recreating the original username with the new password
  5. Signing in as the recreated user and deleting the temporary account

items.title: How many users can I create?
items.text:
There's no hard limit on the number of user accounts. Create as many as needed for your use case.

All enabled users currently have the same DUMB permissions. Creating another account does not create a read-only role.

items.title: "Invalid credentials" error
items.text:
• Check username - Usernames are case-sensitive
  • Verify password - Passwords are also case-sensitive
  • Account status - Check if the user is disabled in Settings

items.title: "User account is disabled" error
items.text: Another authenticated DUMB user has disabled your account. Contact an operator with an enabled account to re-enable it via Settings User Management.

items.title: Session expires too quickly
items.text:
Access tokens expire after 60 minutes by default. Local refresh tokens default to 30 days; OIDC-backed DUMB refresh tokens last one day. If you're experiencing frequent logouts:

  • Check if Remember Me was selected during login
  • Without Remember Me, tokens are stored in session storage and cleared when the browser closes
  • With Remember Me, tokens persist in local storage

items.title: Browser shows login page but I was logged in
items.text:
• Your access token may have expired
  • The frontend should automatically refresh - wait a moment
  • If it persists, clear browser storage and log in again
  • Check if authentication was recently disabled/re-enabled

items.title: How do I disable a user without deleting them?
items.text:
1. Go to Settings User Management
  2. Find the user
  3. Click the disable button

Disabled users cannot log in but their account remains for re-enabling later.

items.title: "Cannot disable the last active user" error
items.text:
DUMB prevents disabling or deleting the last non-disabled user to avoid lockouts. To disable this user:

  1. Create another user account first
  2. Then disable the original user

items.title: How do I delete a user?
items.text:
1. Go to Settings User Management
  2. Find the user
  3. Click the delete button
  4. Confirm the deletion

Permanent action

Deleted users cannot be recovered. Create a new account if needed.

items.title: I forgot my password - how do I reset it?
items.text:
DUMB has no self-service password reset. First try another enabled operator account or the identity provider's recovery tools. If local-account recovery is necessary:

  1. Restrict access to DUMB and stop its container.
  2. Back up the host-mounted /config/users.json privately, preserving the original users, signing secret, and OIDC settings.
  3. In that file, set "enabled": false. If the mode is OIDC-only, temporarily set "mode": "hybrid" so the temporary local account can sign in later; keep the oidc settings intact.
  4. Start the container. Authentication is temporarily disabled for anyone who can reach it.
  5. In Settings → User Management, create a temporary local user with a different username.
  6. Re-enable authentication and sign in as that temporary user.
  7. Delete the forgotten local account and recreate it with the desired username and a new password.
  8. Sign in as the recreated user, remove the temporary user, and restore the intended sign-in mode.
  9. Verify login before restoring wider network access. Retain or dispose of the private recovery copy according to your backup policy.

Disabling authentication alone does not change a password or remove existing accounts. Do not clear the user list or signing secret as a shortcut.

items.title: I deleted all users and can't log in
items.text: Follow the lockout recovery steps above to disable authentication, then create a new user.

items.title: The users.json file is corrupted
items.text: Stop DUMB and preserve the damaged file privately before attempting repair. Prefer restoring a known-good backup that retains users, the signing secret, and any OIDC configuration. If no usable backup exists, creating a fresh authentication configuration resets those identities and sessions; plan that recovery explicitly rather than overwriting the file blindly.

items.title: How long do tokens last?
items.text: Token Type Lifetime Access Token 60 minutes Local refresh token 30 days by default OIDC-backed DUMB refresh token 1 day

items.title: How do I authenticate API requests?
items.text:
Include the access token in the Authorization header:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" http://localhost:3005/api/...

items.title: How do I authenticate WebSocket connections?
items.text:
Pass the token as a query parameter:

ws://localhost:3005/ws/status?token=<your_token>

items.title: My API calls return 401 Unauthorized
items.text:
• Verify the token is included in the Authorization header
  • Check if the token has expired
  • Ensure the format is Bearer <token> (with space)
  • Try getting a new token via login

items.title: Where are passwords stored?
items.text: Passwords are hashed using bcrypt and stored in /config/users.json. The original password is never stored.

items.title: Is the JWT secret secure?
items.text: DUMB generates a signing secret when needed and stores it in /config/users.json. Keep the complete file private; it also contains password hashes and may contain OIDC client credentials.

items.title: Can I use DUMB without HTTPS?
items.text:
Yes, but authentication tokens will be transmitted in plain text. For production deployments exposed to the internet:

  • Use a reverse proxy with HTTPS
  • Or deploy behind a VPN

items.title: Should I disable authentication for local use?
items.text: For truly local/isolated environments (e.g., home lab with no internet exposure), disabling authentication simplifies access. However, if anyone on your network can reach DUMB, consider keeping authentication enabled.

items.title: Related pages
items.text:
• Authentication Feature Guide
  • Authentication API
  • DUMB FAQ

items.title: CLI Debrid FAQ
items.text: Visual guide: Follow CLI Debrid's setup and library workflow.

items.title: What does DUMB start with CLI Debrid?
items.text: The stable/older CLI Debrid workflow includes standalone CLI Battery and Phalanx DB, plus the selected Zurg/rclone provider path. DUMB creates and orders those dependencies during onboarding. The v0.7.29+ pre-release exception is described below.

items.title: Does CLI Debrid v0.7.29 still need a separate CLI Battery process?
items.text:
Not in that upstream pre-release architecture. The v0.7.29 pre-release includes a CLI Battery rewrite that imports Battery as an in-process Python module instead of running its Flask service on port 5001.

DUMB 2.23.0 still uses the standalone Battery dependency. If you deliberately install an upstream layout with the in-process rewrite, disable the standalone Battery service and review whether onboarding or Start Core Service re-enables it. The release backend does not provide the newer installed-layout detection.

items.title: Why is CLI Battery on a separate port?
items.text:
A standalone Battery service is separate from the CLI Debrid interface. DUMB configures the connection automatically, so you should not need to edit its port just to use CLI Debrid.

Geek details: standalone Battery ports and embedded layouts

In the standalone/stable integration, CLI Debrid's UI defaults to 5000 and CLI Battery defaults to 5001. During setup DUMB writes cli_debrid.env.CLI_DEBRID_BATTERY_PORT from the actual cli_battery.port, including any dynamically reassigned port. The upstream v0.7.29 pre-release removes this separate network hop.

items.title: Why do I see HTTP 423 responses?
items.text: CLI Battery uses 423 Locked while a resource is deliberately unavailable or still being prepared. For a standalone layout, confirm CLI Battery and Phalanx are running. Open their service cards and select Service Logs, where available; inspect CLI Debrid's logs too. Review the layout note above if Battery is integrated. Do not change ports or delete data merely because a request returns 423.

items.title: Where are its persistent files and symlinks?
items.text:
• Application data inside the container: /cli_debrid/data (persisted below /data/cli_debrid in the maintained layout)
  • Curated library root: /mnt/debrid/clid_symlinks
  • DUMB log: /cli_debrid/data/logs/debug.log

The raw provider mount path and the curated symlink root serve different purposes; point Arr/media-library imports at the curated root expected by your workflow.

items.title: How should I change symlink layouts?
items.text: Use the service page's Symlinks tools for a dry run, snapshot, retarget, copy, or root migration. Do not bulk-edit link targets first. See Symlink Operations.

items.title: How do I troubleshoot a failed update?
items.text: Check the CLI Debrid update status and service logs, then verify the selected release/branch still exists. DUMB preserves /cli_debrid/data while replacing application code. Use Override + install only when you intentionally want DUMB to reinstall the configured target.

items.title: Related pages
items.text:
• CLI Debrid service guide
  • CLI Battery
  • Phalanx DB
  • Auto-update

items.title: Decypharr FAQ
items.text: Visual guide: Compare Decypharr's setup and library path.

items.title: Which mount mode should I choose?
items.text:
Mode Mount owner DUMB behavior dfs Decypharr DFS Decypharr owns the consolidated mount at mount_path; DUMB supplies the required cache directory when missing. rclone Decypharr embedded rclone Decypharr owns the consolidated mount and rclone settings in its own config/UI. external_rclone DUMB-managed rclone Decypharr starts first to expose WebDAV, then DUMB starts one consolidated rclone mount against /webdav. none No local mount Use Decypharr APIs/WebDAV without asking DUMB to create a mount.

DFS and native Usenet are current stable features; a beta branch toggle is not required to use them.

items.title: Why does external rclone start after Decypharr?
items.text: The rclone instance consumes Decypharr's WebDAV endpoint, so starting rclone first creates a dependency cycle. DUMB starts Decypharr, waits for its WebDAV readiness, then starts the decypharr_enabled rclone instance.

items.title: Where do provider API keys belong?
items.text:
Enter Debrid keys in DUMB onboarding or Decypharr's DUMB Config provider fields, then Save to File. Add Usenet provider accounts in Decypharr's own Embedded UI. Avoid putting secrets into screenshots or support logs.

Geek details: provider-key storage and reconciliation

DUMB persists onboarding keys under decypharr.api_keys for every mount mode. Setup reconciles those keys into Decypharr and uses them when an external-rclone instance must be created.

items.title: How is Usenet connected to an Arr app?
items.text: After adding a Usenet account in Decypharr, open the linked Arr's Embedded UI → Settings → Download Clients. Test the generated decypharr-usenet connection. Debrid downloads use Decypharr's separate qBittorrent-compatible client; test that too if you use both. See the first-start guide for root folders and the final import/playback check.

items.title: Why is DUMB waiting for the wrong old provider mount?
items.text: Legacy configs may contain per-provider folders while current configs use one top-level mount.mount_path. Restart after saving the desired mount_type in DUMB so setup can reconcile config.json. If existing links still target the old layout, preview the Decypharr migration playbook in Symlinks before applying it.

items.title: Why does a source build fail with undefined: storage.Downgrade?
items.text:
Older Decypharr source included a root downgrade.go file that newer revisions removed along with storage.Downgrade. An update that leaves the old root file beside the new packages produces this compiler error. Updating Go alone does not remove the obsolete source file.

Update DUMB to a build containing the Decypharr source cleanup fix, then retry Install configured release/branch/commit on the Decypharr service page. DUMB clears previous source and build artifacts before extracting the selected revision, including obsolete root Go files. This preserves Decypharr's configuration, logs, databases, cache, and existing binary during source cleanup.
