items.title: Service ports
items.text:
These are fresh-configuration defaults, not a report of your running stack. Check the port saved in the dashboard or /config/dumb_config.json before adding a Docker mapping or configuring another application.

The maintained Compose file publishes 3005 only. It serves the dashboard, REST gateway (/api/*), and WebSockets (/ws/*). Embedded UIs use this address too; individual service ports are needed for direct clients and external integrations.

Visual guide: See dashboard access and published-port boundaries.

items.title: DUMB listeners
items.text:
Service Default port Access DUMB Frontend and API gateway 3005 http://<host>:3005; normal entry point DUMB API 8000 Container loopback 127.0.0.1; not published by default Traefik embedded UI proxy 18080 Internal frontend proxy target; direct access requires a mapping Traefik dashboard/API 18081 Entry point plus one; normally consumed internally

Use http://<host>:3005/api/process/processes for REST requests. WebSocket requests use ws://<host>:3005/ws/status without /api. See the API guide.

items.title: Workflow and media services
items.text: Service Default port Purpose / direct path Riven Frontend 3000 Web UI Riven Backend 8080 API CLI Debrid 5000 Web UI CLI Battery 5001 API; separate listener only for versions using the external service Decypharr 8282 Web UI/API InfiniDysk frontend 3000 Web UI InfiniDysk backend 8080 API/WebDAV AltMount 8088 Web UI/API; /live readiness endpoint Plex Media Server 32400 /web Jellyfin 8096 Web UI/API Emby 8096 Web UI/API

items.title: Arr applications and library tools
items.text:
Service Default port Purpose Sonarr 8989 TV Radarr 7878 Movies Lidarr 8686 Music Whisparr 6969 Adult media Prowlarr 9696 Indexers NeutArr 9705 Search automation Profilarr 6868 Profiles and custom formats Seerr 5055 Requests Bazarr 6767 Subtitles Tautulli 8181 Plex monitoring Pulsarr 3003 Watchlist automation Maintainerr 6246 Library rules Zilean 8182 Lookup API

These defaults refer to the first configured instance. A second Sonarr or Radarr often receives 8990 or 7879, but those values are not reserved for a particular instance. See multi-instance configuration.

items.title: Optional access and streaming services
items.text:
Service Default port Notes AIOStreams 3006 /stremio/configure; addon clients need a stable trusted HTTPS base_url mediastorm 7777 /admin Traefik Proxy Admin 3004 Web UI/API Authelia 9091 Identity portal/API Cloudflared None Outbound tunnel connector; no local web UI listener

Use the AIOStreams publishing guide for its public addon address. The embedded /ui/aiostreams address is not its public base_url.

items.title: Storage and database services
items.text:
Service Default port Protocol Zurg 9090 HTTP/WebDAV Phalanx DB 8888 HTTP API PostgreSQL 5432 PostgreSQL, not HTTP pgAdmin 5050 Web UI

A second Zurg instance often receives 9091, which also overlaps Authelia's default. Use the assigned port, not an assumed sequence.

items.title: Port collisions
items.text:
DUMB checks enabled-service ports and can move a conflicting listener to the next available port, then save the result. This includes InfiniDysk frontend/backend ports. Traefik reserves its entry point and dashboard together.

Common default overlaps are:

  • Riven and InfiniDysk: 3000 and 8080.
  • Jellyfin and Emby: 8096.
  • A second Zurg instance and Authelia: 9091.

Docker mappings do not update themselves when an internal listener changes. If a service moves from 8096 to 8097, update its mapping and any direct consumers. Embedded routing uses DUMB's generated service configuration.

items.title: Publish only the listeners you use
items.text:
For example, a stack with direct Plex access can publish:

ports:
  - "3005:3005"   # DUMB dashboard, API gateway, embedded UIs
  - "32400:32400" # Plex clients

Add a service mapping when another application or device needs it. A web UI being available through the dashboard does not expose its native protocol to external clients.

The backend's default 127.0.0.1:8000 listener cannot be exposed by adding 8000:8000 alone. Direct backend access also requires changing dumb.api_service.host. Prefer the existing gateway and follow networking guidance when changing exposure.

DUMB authentication protects its own API and dashboard flows. Direct upstream application ports and published Traefik routes need their own access controls. Docker's published-port firewall behavior also depends on the host; see Docker packet filtering.

items.title: Choose your services
items.text: Start with the workflow you want, then enable its services in onboarding. You do not need every service in this catalog. DUMB runs managed applications as processes inside its container; they share the container's network and mounted paths.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
Choose the result you want first, then add only the services and dependencies that workflow needs.

    A --> C["Build an acquisition workflow"]
    A --> D["Add a supporting tool"]
    B --> E["Media server and library paths"]
    C --> F["Provider, collector, Arr apps and media server"]

You want to… Start with Also review Automate a Debrid library CLI Debrid, Riven, or Decypharr Provider credentials, mounts, and curated library paths Stream a Usenet library InfiniDysk, AltMount, or Decypharr NNTP account limits, indexers, Arr clients, and import strategy Manage movies, TV, or music Radarr, Sonarr, Lidarr, Whisparr Prowlarr, download clients, roots, and profiles Play an existing library Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby Readable media paths, accounts, and hardware acceleration Take requests Seerr or Pulsarr Exact media-server and Arr connections, approvals, and quotas Use Stremio addons AIOStreams Sources and a dedicated public HTTPS addon address Use a separate streaming client mediastorm PostgreSQL and playback-provider accounts Publish selected applications Traefik Proxy Admin Route protection, DNS, HTTPS, and optional Cloudflared

items.title: Service categories
items.text:
• DUMB services: the management API and dashboard.
  • Core services: acquisition, automation, requests, and playback.
  • Dependent services: mounts, databases, and supporting runtimes.
  • Optional services: tools you add for a particular workflow.

These categories describe DUMB's service model. An optional service can still be essential to your chosen workflow; disabling it may break clients that use it.

items.title: Core services
items.text: Choose core services around the library workflow you want. A media server can use files you already own; a download workflow usually also needs provider accounts, library paths, and one or more dependencies.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
A complete media workflow connects acquisition, a curated library folder and playback. Use only the parts you need.

flowchart TD
    A["Request or search"] --> B["Chosen acquisition workflow"]
    B --> C["Curated library folder"]
    C --> D["Plex, Jellyfin or Emby"]
    D --> E["Play and verify"]

Several core services can run together. Check shared paths, provider connection limits, and assigned ports before adding a second workflow.

items.text: Service Description Depends On Optional Integrations CLI Debrid Debrid media scraper, automation engine, and upgrade engine CLI Battery for standalone upstream layouts; Phalanx DB, rclone, Zurg Zilean Decypharr Debrid and native Usenet workflow service for Arrs, symlinks, and WebDAV access rclone when external mount mode is used Zilean, Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr InfiniDysk Usenet WebDAV and Arr download-client workflow rclone for the default 1.x integration Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr AltMount Usenet streaming, WebDAV, and SABnzbd-compatible Arr workflow NNTP provider account Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr Plex Hosts media collected by core services Jellyfin Media server for hosting and playing content Emby Media server for hosting and playing content Seerr Media request and discovery platform Plex, Radarr, Sonarr Riven Backend Debrid media scraper and automation engine PostgreSQL; stable mode also uses rclone and Zurg Zilean, Riven Frontend Sonarr TV automation and organization Prowlarr, Decypharr, InfiniDysk, AltMount Radarr Movie automation and organization Prowlarr, Decypharr, InfiniDysk, AltMount Lidarr Music automation and organization Prowlarr, Decypharr, InfiniDysk, AltMount Prowlarr Indexer manager for Arrs Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr Whisparr Adult content automation and organization Prowlarr, Decypharr, InfiniDysk, AltMount NeutArr Continuous backlog searches for Arr instances Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr Profilarr Profiles and formats manager for Sonarr/Radarr Sonarr, Radarr

items.title: Dependency guidelines
items.text:
• Enable dependencies required by the installed service layout. DUMB orders managed dependencies during startup.
  • Keep raw provider mounts separate from curated library roots. Media servers must resolve the paths used by symlinks.
  • Use each Arr instance's core_service setting to select its workflow. Review routing rules before combining clients.

A running process does not confirm a working import or playback path.

items.title: AltMount (Core Service)
items.text:
AltMount connects your Usenet accounts to Sonarr, Radarr and your media server. Its web interface handles provider accounts, queues, content access and the way completed items enter your library.

In DUMB, AltMount is a core Usenet workflow service. DUMB installs and starts AltMount, supplies its baseline configuration, embeds its UI, and connects enabled Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and Whisparr instances whose core_service includes altmount.

items.title: First-start checklist
items.text:
1. Select AltMount and your intended Arr applications during DUMB onboarding, then choose the mount mode. Reopen onboarding from Settings → Launch Onboarding if needed.
  2. Open the AltMount service card. On DUMB Config, use Start if stopped, then select Embedded UI. Create the first administrator in AltMount or sign in to the existing account.
  3. Replace first-run WebDAV credentials before exposing the endpoint outside a trusted network. Update dependent clients and restart the affected mount when needed.
  4. Add and test at least one TLS-enabled Usenet provider account. Review the selected mount type and path in AltMount's Mount settings; shared accounts must stay within their total connection allowance.
  5. Open AltMount → Configuration → Import. Choose NONE, SYMLINK or STRM and prepare any required import directory. This choice is separate from the mount mode. Follow Import strategy and library paths before sending a real item.
  6. In each Arr's Embedded UI, test the altmount entry under Settings → Download Clients, then test its indexers. Review Settings → Media Management → Root Folders and add that same library folder to your media server.
  7. Send one small intended NZB. Follow the queue through import, scan the media library and play it. A successful provider test alone does not check library visibility or playback.

items.title: Workflow diagram
items.text:
Sign in, test your Usenet account, and finish the import and library choices before testing a real item. Geek details: how requests, providers, mounts and libraries connect

The dashed arrows are DUMB automation. The solid arrows are the normal request and media flow after setup.

items.title: Service relationships
items.text:
AltMount uses your Usenet provider accounts and connects to the Arr applications you select. Prowlarr can supply indexers; Plex, Jellyfin or Emby plays the resulting library. A usable Usenet provider account is required.

Geek details: service classification and runtime dependencies Classification Role Core Service Usenet WebDAV, streaming, and Arr download-client workflow DUMB Dependencies None by default; PostgreSQL is enabled only for an optional database cutover External Requirement At least one usable NNTP provider account Integrates With Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr, Prowlarr, request services, and media servers Exposes UI Yes, on the configured AltMount port and through DUMB's embedded UI

external_rclone does not create or start a DUMB-managed rclone instance. In that mode AltMount exposes its rclone RC service, while you remain responsible for the external mount process.

items.title: What AltMount provides
items.text:
Use AltMount's web interface to add providers, watch its queue and choose how imported items enter your library. It supports multiple provider accounts and several library styles, including direct mounted folders, symlinks and .strm files. Review the import choice below before sending a real request.

Geek details: streaming protocols, content access and processing features
  • A web UI and API for configuration, queue visibility, and health monitoring
  • WebDAV access and range-based streaming directly from Usenet
  • A SABnzbd-compatible download-client API for Arr applications
  • Multiple NNTP providers with load distribution and failover
  • Transparent handling of NZB content and supported archive formats
  • NONE, SYMLINK, and STRM import strategies
  • Built-in FUSE and rclone mount modes, plus an external-rclone mode
  • Local metadata with optional SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration through DUMB

AltMount owns the media-processing behavior. DUMB supplies the service lifecycle and integration around it.

items.title: What DUMB manages
items.text:
DUMB installs and starts AltMount, keeps your selected mount arrangement in sync, and creates the selected Arr connections. You manage administrator access, provider accounts, import settings and media-library folders in the applications' own interfaces.

Keep mount choices in DUMB's settings and import choices in AltMount. DUMB reapplies its managed connection and mount settings during setup, so review the selections there before changing them elsewhere.

Geek details: generated secrets, authoritative fields and integration ownership DUMB manages You manage in AltMount Downloads the architecture-specific release binary and records its version Administrator credentials and application access policy Creates config, metadata, log, rclone, and mount directories Provider accounts, connection allocation, and TLS policy Generates JWT_SECRET and ALTMOUNT_API_KEY when missing WebDAV credentials, external clients, and public/proxy settings Maps DUMB's mount choice into AltMount's native mount_type Import strategy, import directory, streaming cache, health monitoring, and advanced provider behavior Enables SABnzbd compatibility and adds standard media categories Arr root folders, media-server library paths, and validation of the complete import path Adds linked Arr instances to AltMount and adds AltMount as their download client Optional AltMount webhooks and any tuning beyond DUMB's baseline Proxies the root-style web application into the service page AltMount user accounts and application-level access policy

DUMB preserves most AltMount settings, but some fields are authoritative

DUMB creates /altmount/config.yaml only when the file is missing. On later setup or restart passes, it preserves providers and other AltMount-owned settings while synchronizing the DUMB-managed mount path/type, rclone mode, API prefix/key, SABnzbd enablement/categories, and Arr integration structure.

Geek details: alternative direct URLs, health probes and embedded routes Technical details: configuration reference

items.title: Default port and URLs
items.text:
Endpoint Default Purpose Native listener 8088 AltMount web UI, WebDAV, SABnzbd-compatible API, and application API Health probe http://127.0.0.1:8088/live Used by DUMB while completing post-start Arr integration DUMB embedded route /service/ui/altmount Traefik-backed service UI route Frontend iframe route /ui/altmount Internal dmbdb iframe/proxy context; open it from the AltMount service page

The native port is inside the DUMB container. It is directly reachable from the host only if your deployment publishes or otherwise exposes it.

items.title: Configuration in dumb_config.json
items.text:
The current default block is:

{
"altmount": {
  "enabled": false,
  "postgres_enabled": false,
  "postgres_database": "",
  "process_name": "AltMount",
  "repo_owner": "javi11",
  "repo_name": "altmount",
  "pinned_version": "latest",
  "suppress_logging": false,
  "log_level": "INFO",
  "port": 8088,
  "auto_update": false,
  "auto_update_interval": 24,
  "auto_update_start_time": "04:00",
  "mount_type": "rclone",
  "config_dir": "/altmount",
  "config_file": "/altmount/config.yaml",
  "metadata_dir": "/altmount/metadata",
  "mount_path": "/mnt/debrid/altmount",
  "log_file": "/altmount/logs/altmount.log",
  "command": [
    "/altmount/altmount",
    "serve",
    "--config",
    "/altmount/config.yaml"
  ],
  "env": {
    "PUID": "{puid}",
    "PGID": "{pgid}",
    "PORT": "{port}",
    "JWT_SECRET": "",
    "COOKIE_DOMAIN": "localhost",
    "ALTMOUNT_API_KEY": ""
  }
}
}

items.title: Important fields
items.text:
• enabled: Starts AltMount under DUMB's process manager.
  • pinned_version: Uses the latest upstream release or a specific release tag. DUMB installs the matching architecture-specific altmount-cli asset.
  • port: Sets the native AltMount listener and is copied into env.PORT.
  • mount_type: Selects DUMB's operator-facing mount mode.
  • mount_path: Shared path where the selected internal mount is exposed; DUMB synchronizes this into AltMount's root-level configuration.
  • config_dir, config_file, metadata_dir, log_file: Persistent paths managed by DUMB.
  • auto_update, auto_update_interval, auto_update_start_time: Use DUMB's normal update scheduler.
  • postgres_enabled, postgres_database: Select the optional PostgreSQL backend after completing the guarded migration workflow.
  • env.JWT_SECRET, env.ALTMOUNT_API_KEY: Generated and saved by DUMB when blank. Treat both as secrets.
  • env.COOKIE_DOMAIN: Defaults to localhost; change it only when your direct or reverse-proxied AltMount access model requires another cookie domain.

command, PUID, PGID, and PORT are reconciled by setup. Avoid treating them as independent AltMount UI settings.

items.title: Mount modes
items.text:
Choose the mount mode during onboarding or on AltMount's DUMB Config. The normal rclone choice lets AltMount make content available as a folder. Native FUSE is another managed folder option; external_rclone requires an operator-managed mount, and none leaves local mounting to other clients. Keep a working existing path until its consumers and migration have been reviewed.

Mount mode makes content accessible. The import strategy below decides what the Arr application imports; changing one does not complete the other.

Geek details: mount-mode mapping, external ownership and stale-mount handling DUMB value AltMount value Behavior dfs fuse AltMount's native FUSE mount at mount_path rclone rclone Default; AltMount starts its built-in rclone mount and RC service external_rclone rclone_external AltMount starts the RC service but does not mount; you provide the external rclone process none none AltMount does not start a FUSE or rclone mount; WebDAV remains available

DUMB creates /mnt/debrid/altmount by default and normalizes its ownership. During an install/update pass, DUMB also unmounts a stale FUSE mount at that exact path before replacing the AltMount binary. A non-FUSE mount is preserved rather than removed automatically.

Mount mode and import strategy are different decisions

mount_type controls how AltMount content becomes visible as a filesystem. The AltMount-owned import strategy controls what Arr imports from that content.

items.title: Import strategy and library paths
items.text:
Configure the import strategy in AltMount → Configuration → Import:

Strategy Behavior Typical use NONE Arr reads directly from the mounted content Simplest direct-mount workflow SYMLINK AltMount creates category-based links in an import directory Upstream's recommended choice for most Arr workflows STRM AltMount writes .strm files that point to WebDAV URLs Common with Emby/Jellyfin or URL-based playback

DUMB does not currently choose the import strategy, create its import_dir, or set Arr root folders/media-server libraries for AltMount. Keep every path inside the shared DUMB namespace—normally under /mnt/debrid—and make sure AltMount, the linked Arr, and the media server all see the same container path.

For SYMLINK or STRM, create and validate the chosen import directory before sending a real release. For NONE, confirm the linked Arr can browse the mounted category path under /mnt/debrid/altmount.

See AltMount's ARR integration guide for the application-level import and webhook options.

items.title: DUMB-to-AltMount Arr integration
items.text:
Select AltMount for the intended Arr instances during onboarding. For an existing instance, open its DUMB Config, include altmount in its core_service selection, and Save to File. After both services are running, test the generated altmount client in the Arr application. Merely starting an Arr does not assign it to AltMount.

Geek details: manual Arr workflow selection and automatic client wiring

For an enabled Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, or Whisparr instance, set:

{
"core_service": "altmount"
}

For a shared Arr instance that uses several workflow services, use a list or the equivalent comma-separated UI selection:

{
"core_service": ["decypharr", "infinidysk", "altmount"]
}

During guided onboarding, DUMB then:

  1. Installs/configures AltMount and generates its internal secrets if needed.
  2. Starts the selected Arr services and AltMount.
  3. Reads each linked Arr API key from its application config.
  4. Upserts the Arr instance URL/API key into AltMount's arrs section.
  5. Enables AltMount's SABnzbd-compatible API and standard categories (movies, tv, music, and adult).
  6. Creates or updates an altmount SABnzbd download client in each linked Arr with the matching category.

The core_service selection scopes normal Arr integration. Review the exact native entries after setup; enabling an Arr process alone does not assign it to AltMount.

Finish the AltMount-owned setup

A new native configuration starts with providers empty. Configure and test the required NNTP accounts in AltMount. Choose and validate the import strategy, confirm the Arr root/import paths, and test playback before relying on automation.

items.title: AIOStreams playback
items.text:
AIOStreams can send matching NZBs to AltMount's SABnzbd-compatible API and serve the resulting WebDAV stream:

  1. Enable AltMount's SAB API and copy its API key.
  2. Create dedicated WebDAV credentials.
  3. In AIOStreams, add AltMount under Services.
  4. Use http://127.0.0.1:8088 for URL, replacing 8088 with AltMount's saved DUMB port.
  5. Enter the API key and WebDAV credentials.
  6. Prefer leaving Public URL blank and supplying an AIOStreams auth credential (username:password) whose user has Proxy permission. Use a direct Public URL only when AltMount has its own trusted HTTPS origin reachable by the player.

This does not change AltMount's DUMB-selected mount mode or Arr import strategy. AIOStreams communicates with the application API and WebDAV surface directly; never use its embedded /ui/altmount route as the service URL.

items.title: PostgreSQL migration
items.text:
SQLite is the default and needs no separate database setup. To move an existing library to PostgreSQL, open Database Migration on the AltMount service page. Run a rehearsal, review the imported table counts, then use guarded cutover and check AltMount afterward.

Do not enable postgres_enabled directly when existing data must be retained. Back up the service and follow SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration.

Geek details: database files, connection configuration and rollback artifacts

AltMount supports SQLite and PostgreSQL. New/default installs use /altmount/altmount.db.

For an existing SQLite-backed service, open Database Migration on the AltMount service page, run a rehearsal, validate the imported table counts against AltMount's application-created PostgreSQL schema, and only then run cutover. DUMB writes the PostgreSQL DSN into /altmount/config.yaml, registers the target database (altmount by default), and retains the SQLite file and migration backups for rollback.

Do not enable postgres_enabled directly when existing data must be retained. DUMB has not found an upstream application-specific data migration tool, so the guarded DUMB workflow and post-cutover application checks are important. See SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration.

Geek details: PostgreSQL schema compatibility handling

AltMount v0.3.2 migration compatibility

AltMount v0.3.2 contains invalid PostgreSQL syntax in its bundled migration 10 expression index. DUMB applies the intended index only in an isolated staging database whose latest Goose version is exactly 9 and which contains the expected import_queue.metadata column. Any mismatch refuses the repair and restores SQLite instead of skipping unknown schema work.

items.title: Back up AltMount
items.text:
Keep an independent backup before updates or migrations. AltMount's application data contains account credentials, keys and library metadata, so keep the backup private.

Geek details: installed files and persistence paths Path Purpose /altmount/altmount DUMB-installed release binary /altmount/config.yaml AltMount runtime configuration, including provider credentials /altmount/altmount.db Default SQLite database /altmount/metadata NZB metadata root /altmount/rclone AltMount's managed rclone files/state /altmount/logs/altmount.log AltMount application log /altmount/version.txt DUMB-managed installed-version marker /mnt/debrid/altmount Default selected mount path

In the maintained Compose layout, back up /data/altmount (the persistence target behind internal /altmount) as sensitive application data. It can contain NNTP credentials, API keys, user data, and the SQLite database.

items.title: Embedded UI behavior
items.text:
Geek details: embedded UI routing

AltMount is a root-route React-style application. dmbdb keeps its root navigation and root /api/* calls in the AltMount iframe context so they do not collide with DUMB's own application or API routes. Open the UI from the AltMount service page rather than browsing directly to /ui/altmount.

If the embedded UI loses routing context, reload the DUMB service page. The direct Traefik-backed route is /service/ui/altmount when embedded service UIs are enabled.

items.title: AltMount does not start
items.text:
Open AltMount's DUMB Config to check its status, then Service Logs for the first error. Keep that error with your support request. If you recently changed a port, mount or import path, review the saved change before retrying startup.

Geek details: diagnose executable, configuration and mount failures

items.title: Host and filesystem checks
items.text:
• Check the DUMB service log and /altmount/logs/altmount.log.
  • Confirm /altmount/altmount exists and is executable.
  • Verify the configured port is free and /altmount/config.yaml is valid YAML.
  • For FUSE/rclone modes, check whether /mnt/debrid/altmount is a stale, dangling, read-only, or busy mount path.

items.title: Provider or streaming failures
items.text:
• Confirm at least one provider is enabled and its credentials, TLS mode, and connection limit are valid.
  • Do not allocate more combined connections than the provider account permits.
  • Review AltMount's queue and health pages for missing articles, masked files, or cache pressure.

items.title: Arr download-client setup is missing
items.text:
Check that both services are running and AltMount is selected for the Arr instance in DUMB Config. Open the Arr's Embedded UI → Settings → Download Clients and test altmount. If it is still missing after guided setup, save the relevant service-log errors for support.

Geek details: inspect integration secrets, category selection and retries

items.title: Arr integration checks
items.text:
• Confirm the Arr instance is enabled and core_service includes altmount.
  • Confirm DUMB can read the Arr API key and AltMount's generated ALTMOUNT_API_KEY is still present.
  • Verify both services are running, then restart AltMount or rerun the guided start so DUMB can repeat the integration pass.
  • Check that the Arr category matches the DUMB defaults for its application type.

items.title: Import completes but the library cannot see the file
items.text:
• Confirm mount_path, the AltMount import_dir, the Arr root folder, and the media-server library use paths visible inside the DUMB container.
  • For SYMLINK, inspect the link target from inside the container and verify it remains under a shared path.
  • For STRM, confirm the WebDAV URL written into the file is reachable by the player.
  • Use Arr Manual Import to separate path visibility problems from download-client problems.

items.title: Embedded UI/API requests open DUMB instead of AltMount
items.text:
Reload the DUMB service page and reopen Embedded UI. If the issue continues, keep the browser error and service-log details for support.

Geek details: inspect embedded-route context and proxy logs

items.title: Proxy-route diagnostics
items.text:
• Reopen the AltMount service page and reload the iframe to refresh dumb_ui_service context.
  • Verify embedded service UIs are enabled and /service/ui/altmount responds.
  • Check dmbdb proxy logs for root-route or /api/* routing errors.

items.title: CLI Debrid (Core Service)
items.text:
CLI Debrid acquires and upgrades media through Debrid providers. Configure content sources, scrapers, provider credentials, and library paths in CLI Debrid after DUMB installs its runtime and selected dependencies.

For an upstream CLI Debrid layout with embedded Battery, DUMB 2.23.0 does not detect the replacement automatically. Review the CLI Debrid FAQ before enabling that layout.

items.title: First start
items.text:
1. Choose CLI Debrid in DUMB onboarding and select its provider, supporting services and library paths. Reopen onboarding with Settings → Launch Onboarding if needed.
  2. Open the CLI Debrid service card. Wait for its selected supporting services to start; on DUMB Config, choose Start if CLI Debrid is stopped. Select Embedded UI to open its setup interface.
  3. Authorize the accounts you use. Choose your content sources, which tell CLI Debrid what you want, and scrapers, which find matching sources. Review quality and collection rules before enabling large lists.
  4. Review Original Files Path and the collection mode in CLI Debrid. Use Symlinked/Local if it should create an organized linked library; use Plex if it should monitor the chosen Plex libraries. See Mount Considerations for screenshots and the path checks.
  5. Add the chosen organized library folder to your media server. If using Plex authorization, configure and start Plex first, then verify the saved Plex URL remains reachable.
  6. Add one intended item to your chosen source. Watch it progress through the queues, confirm it appears in the expected media library, and play it before importing large lists.

Check the CLI Battery layout note above before selecting an upstream development release. A running CLI Debrid service does not prove that its sources, scrapers and library are ready.

items.title: Service Relationships
items.text:
CLI Debrid collects items from the sources you choose and organizes them for your media server. Its selected supporting services start through DUMB; Zilean is an optional scraper. Keep dependencies enabled for the installed CLI Debrid layout described above.

Geek details: service classification and runtime dependencies Classification Role Core Service Debrid Orchestrator Depends On Stable/older releases: CLI Battery; provider path: rclone and Zurg Optional Phalanx DB, Zilean Exposes UI Yes (Flask app on port 5000) Technical details: configuration reference

items.title: Key configuration fields
items.text:
• enabled: Toggle to run CLI Debrid via DUMB.
  • process_name: Used for display and logs.
  • repo_owner, repo_name: GitHub repo to use for updates.
  • release_version_enabled, branch_enabled: Target a specific tag or branch.
  • commit_sha: Build an exact CLI Debrid revision from its full 40-character GitHub SHA.
  • log_level, suppress_logging: Logging controls.
  • port: Flask web interface port.
  • env: Environment variable configuration used by CLI Debrid.
  • env.CLI_DEBRID_BATTERY_PORT: Battery API port consumed by standalone CLI Debrid layouts. It is not present in the untouched template; DUMB creates/synchronizes it from cli_battery.port during setup and config updates. The embedded layout does not use this network hop.
  • clear_on_update, exclude_dirs: Clean old files during update while protecting data dirs.

items.title: Intelligent Automation
items.text:
• Monitors your Plex library or local folder structure (symlinked library)
  • Scrapes for content from various sources (Zilean, Jackett, Torrentio, Nyaa, Media Fusion)
  • Downloads new or upgraded content using Debrid providers
  • Optionally leverages webhook notifications from Seerr or Zurg to trigger updates

items.title: Supported Features
items.text:
• Content Sources: MDBList, Trakt, Seerr
  • Upgrading: Queue system for quality upgrades
  • Web UI: Web dashboard for real-time monitoring and control
  • Metadata: Cached locally in the cli_battery
  • Notifications: Optional support for Discord, Email, Telegram, NTFY
  • Scraping Tuning: Manual test interface to evaluate scraper priorities

items.title: Standalone CLI Battery
items.text:
Required only by layouts that still use the standalone service

Keep CLI Battery enabled for installed CLI Debrid layouts that call its API on port 5001. See the layout guidance near the top of this page before selecting an upstream version that embeds Battery.

items.title: Mount Considerations
items.text:
CLI Debrid can create symlinks to be used in the media server, or if using the rclone mounts directly in the media server it can monitor the Plex libraries for completed items.

In both cases, ensure the appropriate path for the rclone or zurg mount is used when adding the Original Files Path.

Original Files Path

The Original Files Path is relative to the paths inside the container.

Example: As default when configured with the onboarding process, the rclone mount_dir is set to /mnt/debrid, the rclone mount_name is set to clid, and it is using zurg_enabled: true for rclone, then the path should be:

As mentioned, CLI Debrid also monitors either the created symlinks or the Plex libraries for completed items.

As such, it's important to ensure you select the appropriate option for your deployment.

Collection Mode Selection

Symlinked/Local will create symlinks in the user defined path, whereas Plex will monitor the Plex Libraries defined and not create symlinks.

items.title: Symlink repair and migration
items.text:
For the complete DUMB symlink guide (UI option behavior, root scope, backup/restore, schedule, retention, and migration playbooks), see Symlink Operations.

Use Symlink Operations for the frontend repair and backup controls. Preview changes to the selected CLI Debrid library, review the proposed targets and retain a manifest before applying repairs. You only need this when maintaining or moving an existing library.

Geek details: API repairs, root migration and scheduled manifests

For CLI Debrid symlink libraries (commonly /mnt/debrid/clid_symlinks), DUMB exposes POST /api/process/symlink-repair to rewrite symlink targets after mount-path changes.

Example custom rewrite for CLI Debrid:

{
  "dry_run": true,
  "roots": ["/mnt/debrid/clid_symlinks"],
  "rewrite_rules": [
    {
      "from_prefix": "/mnt/debrid/clid_old",
      "to_prefix": "/mnt/debrid/clid"
    }
  ]
}

Set "dry_run": false to apply and optionally set backup_path for a manifest.

If you need to move the symlink tree itself (not just rewrite targets), use root_migrations:

{
  "dry_run": false,
  "root_migrations": [
    {
      "from_root": "/mnt/debrid/clid_symlinks_old",
      "to_root": "/mnt/debrid/clid_symlinks"
    }
  ]
}

If you want to populate another service symlink tree without removing CLI Debrid entries (for example /mnt/debrid/clid_symlinks to /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks), include "copy_instead_of_move": true in the same request.

For recurring backups of existing symlink libraries, use service config keys symlink_backup_enabled, symlink_backup_interval, symlink_backup_start_time, and symlink_backup_path to enable DUMB’s internal scheduler. Keep generated manifests for POST /api/process/symlink-manifest/restore recovery runs. Use symlink_backup_retention_count to keep only the newest N scheduled manifests (0 keeps all).

items.title: Plex Media Server Built-in!
items.text:
With Plex Media Server enabled in DUMB, you can also leverage it with CLI Debrid.

As shown below, if you select to "Sign in to Plex" during the CLI Debrid onboarding, it will allow you to select the local instance of Plex Media Server.

Plex Media Server Requirement

Plex Media Server must be configured and running in DUMB before it will appear in the list of available servers.

Signing into Plex and selecting the DUMB Plex Media Server will pre-populate the "Plex URL" and "Plex Token" within the CLI Debrid onboarding.

Plex URL Configuration

However, note that it sets the "Plex URL" as the DUMB docker container's IP Address:

This may cause issues if the address changes for the container, so it is suggested to change the "Plex URL" as shown below:

items.title: Zilean Built-in!
items.text: With Zilean enabled in DUMB, you can also leverage it with CLI Debrid

items.title: Check request progress
items.text:
Open CLI Debrid's queue views to follow your test item. Wanted and Scraping mean a source is still being found; Adding and Checking mean the item is being sent to the provider or checked for collection. Review the item's status when progress stops. An unreleased item may simply be waiting for its release, while an uncached item may need time or available account capacity.

If the item is collected but missing from Plex, compare the saved collection folder with the Plex library folder and check the library scan. Avoid re-adding a large list while diagnosing one item.

Geek details: queue scheduling, state transitions and webhook integration

items.title: Queues & Processing (Behind the Scenes)
items.text:
• Wanted Queue: Items identified from your lists that need to be downloaded but haven't been processed by the scraper yet. Shows the time the item was last scraped. If within 24 hours of scraping items will remain in the Wanted queue.
  • Scraping Queue: Items actively being searched for download sources (torrents/magnets).
  • Adding Queue: Items for which a source has been found and are being added to your debrid service

  • Checking Queue: Monitoring items for presence locally or in Plex.

    • Cached: Available in debrid cache and ready to use.

    • Downloading: Currently being downloaded with progress shown; grouped if multiple files.

    • Filenames: Can be toggled to show specific files being processed

  • Unreleased: Items identified but waiting for their release date before processing continues. Displays the relevant release date(s). Items requiring a physical release will indicate this.

  • Blacklisting: Items that have been explicitly marked to be ignored by the application.
  • Upgrading Queue: Items that are being considered for Upgrading. They have been collected and now for 24 hours cli_debrid will try to find upgrades once an hour.
  • Final Check: Items for which initial scraping attempts failed. These items wait for a configured delay (defined in settings) before one last search attempt is automatically triggered. Shows when the item entered this waiting period. If the final search is successful, the item moves to Adding. If it fails again, the item is typically moved to Blacklisted.
  • Pending Uncached: Items associated with uncached torrents that would take your account over its limit wait in the Pending Uncached queue until your download limit returns to normal.
  • Sleeping Queue: Items that cli_debrid failed to find. Shows a 'Wake Count' indicating how many times the item has been retried.

All queues are managed on scheduled intervals.

items.title: Webhook Support
items.text:
CLI Debrid can listen for:

  • Seerr Webhooks: Add content when users request it
  • Zurg Webhooks: React to completed downloads (Symlink mode)
Geek details: configure a Zurg webhook script

Example Zurg update hook:

#!/bin/bash
webhook_url="http://localhost:5000/webhook/rclone"
for arg in "$@"
do
  encoded=$(echo -n "$arg" | python3 -c "import sys, urllib.parse as ul; print(ul.quote(sys.stdin.read()))")
  curl -s -X GET "$webhook_url?file=$encoded"
done
echo "Webhook update complete."

items.title: Service updates
items.text:

items.title: Decypharr (Core Service)
items.text: Decypharr connects Sonarr and Radarr to Debrid providers, Usenet providers, or both. Use DUMB to select and start the workflow, then use Decypharr to review providers and queues. The instructions below cover a new setup; existing libraries also need a path and backup review before changes.

items.title: First start
items.text:
1. Choose Decypharr in DUMB onboarding and select Debrid, Usenet, or both. Select the Arr applications and media server that will use it. Reopen onboarding from Settings → Launch Onboarding when needed.
  2. Enter the Debrid account API keys you intend to use and choose the mount mode. For a new Decypharr-managed filesystem, dfs is the recommended default. Existing libraries should retain their current paths until a migration is planned.
  3. Open the Decypharr service card. On DUMB Config, choose Start if stopped, then open Embedded UI. Review the provider configuration. For Usenet, add and test your NNTP account in Decypharr; a Debrid key does not replace that account.
  4. Open Sonarr or Radarr's Embedded UI → Settings → Download Clients and test the generated Decypharr client. A Debrid client uses the qBittorrent-compatible connection; Usenet uses the SABnzbd-compatible connection. Test indexers under Settings → Indexers too.
  5. Review Settings → Media Management → Root Folders in each Arr. Use the saved curated folder as the corresponding media-server library source. See root folders for Decypharr-only and combined paths.
  6. Request one intended item and follow its Arr queue through import. Scan the media-server library and play it before enabling broad acquisition.

For an existing library, preview Symlink Operations before changing mount paths. Keep a backup and review the preview before applying a repair.

Protect provider credentials

Debrid API keys and Usenet credentials grant access to your accounts. Keep them private and do not include them in shared screenshots or logs.

items.title: Key configuration fields
items.text:
• enabled: Toggle to run Decypharr via DUMB.
  • process_name: Used for display and logs.
  • repo_owner, repo_name: GitHub repo to use for updates.
  • release_version_enabled, branch_enabled: Target a specific tag or branch.
  • commit_sha: Build an exact Decypharr source revision from its full 40-character GitHub SHA.
  • log_level, suppress_logging: Logging controls.
  • port: Web UI port.
  • env: Environment variables passed to Decypharr.
  • mount_type: Decypharr mount mode. Stable Decypharr 2.0+ supports dfs, rclone, external_rclone, and none without requiring the beta branch.
  • mount_path: Container path for the Decypharr mount (default /mnt/debrid/decypharr).
  • api_keys: Per-provider API keys used by Decypharr for Debrid providers.
  • clear_on_update, exclude_dirs: Clean old files during update while protecting data dirs.

Because release_version_enabled is false, the stored v1.0.0 value is only the fallback selector; normal stable installs resolve the latest supported GitHub release. Enable the selector only when intentionally pinning a release.

Exact commit pin

Set commit_sha to a full 40-character SHA to build that immutable Decypharr revision. The commit pin overrides release and branch settings, uses Decypharr's source-build path, and disables automatic updates until changed or cleared.

items.title: What Decypharr does
items.text:
Use Decypharr's web interface to review providers and the queue. Linked Arr applications request content and organize it into the root folders you selected. The media server should scan those curated folders.

Geek details: download-client compatibility and processing features

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
Decypharr acts as both a torrent manager and a renaming/organizing engine:

  • Handles torrent links via Debrid services
  • Handles NZB/Usenet downloads through Decypharr 2.0+ native Usenet support
  • Mimics qBittorrent and Sabnzbd-compatible APIs for Arr download-client integration
  • Renames and organizes files into structured symlink folders
  • Provides a Web UI and WebDAV endpoints for remote management

items.title: Supported Features
items.text:
• Mock Qbittorrent API for Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, etc.
  • Full-featured UI for managing torrents
  • Proxy filtering for un-cached Debrid torrents
  • Multiple Debrid service support (Real Debrid, Torbox, Debrid Link, All Debrid, Premiumize)
  • WebDAV server per Debrid provider for mounting remote files
  • DFS mount mode for Decypharr-managed streaming paths (stable in Decypharr 2.0+)
  • Native Usenet support through Decypharr's Sabnzbd-compatible endpoint (stable in Decypharr 2.0+)
  • Repair Worker for missing files or symlinks

items.title: Integration with DUMB
items.text:
Select the intended Arr applications during onboarding. Test the generated clients and saved folders in their own interfaces before adding broad automation. The maintenance steps below apply when moving or repairing an existing library.

Geek details: how DUMB generates Decypharr and Arr settings

When Decypharr starts, DUMB performs several automation steps:

  • Writes the selected Debrid provider, API key, download folder, and mount settings to the current Decypharr config schema before the first process launch
  • Syncs Arr instance details into config.json
  • Ensures /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/<instance> roots exist
  • Updates Arr permissions and root folders
  • Adds or updates a qBittorrent-style download client named decypharr in Arr
  • Populates Debrid providers from api_keys for Decypharr mount modes
  • Uses per-instance category labels when creating Arr download client entries
  • Adds a Sabnzbd-style download client named decypharr-usenet when Decypharr Usenet providers are configured

When Decypharr is installed through DUMB onboarding, this pre-start configuration satisfies Decypharr's own first-run checks. You should land in the normal Decypharr UI instead of being asked to repeat its standalone setup wizard. The Decypharr wizard remains useful for installations managed outside DUMB.

items.title: Symlink repair and migration
items.text:
For the complete DUMB symlink guide (UI option behavior, root scope, backup/restore, schedule, retention, and migration playbooks), see Symlink Operations.

Open Symlink Operations for the frontend repair, backup and restore workflow. Preview the affected library roots first, then review the proposed changes and keep a recovery manifest before applying them. This is a library maintenance task, not part of a new setup.

Geek details: repair or migrate links through the API

If mount layouts change (for example provider-path changes between Decypharr modes), use POST /api/process/symlink-repair to rewrite existing symlink targets instead of manually relinking.

Common Decypharr migration:

{
  "dry_run": true,
  "presets": ["decypharr_beta_consolidated"]
}

Apply changes:

{
  "dry_run": false,
  "presets": ["decypharr_beta_consolidated"],
  "backup_path": "/config/symlink-repair/decypharr-manifest.json"
}

When Arr core_service changes from Decypharr-only to combined Decypharr+InfiniDysk, root folders move from /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/<slug> to /mnt/debrid/combined_symlinks/<slug>. Use root migration mode:

{
  "dry_run": false,
  "root_migrations": [
    {
      "from_root": "/mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks",
      "to_root": "/mnt/debrid/combined_symlinks"
    }
  ],
  "backup_path": "/config/symlink-repair/decypharr-combined-manifest.json"
}

To clone entries into the new root while keeping the old root intact (for staged imports), set "copy_instead_of_move": true.

For periodic safety snapshots, set service config keys symlink_backup_enabled, symlink_backup_interval, symlink_backup_start_time, and symlink_backup_path to let DUMB run internal scheduled snapshots. You can also run/manual restore via POST /api/process/symlink-manifest/backup and POST /api/process/symlink-manifest/restore. Set symlink_backup_retention_count to keep only the newest N scheduled manifests (0 disables pruning).

Startup timing

If the Decypharr UI is not reachable yet, DUMB retries the download-client setup shortly after startup.

Download client credentials

DUMB configures the Arr qBittorrent download client to point at 127.0.0.1:<port> and uses the Arr host/API key as the username/password pair expected by Decypharr.

Geek details: select workflow services with JSON

items.title: Arr core_service setting
items.text:
For Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr/Whisparr instances you want wired to Decypharr, set core_service to decypharr or include it in a list:

{
"core_service": "decypharr"
}

{
"core_service": ["decypharr", "infinidysk", "altmount"]
}

This tells DUMB to auto-configure Arr integration around Decypharr’s WebDAV and symlink workflows. See Core Service Routing for how core_service affects automation.

To successfully run Decypharr with DUMB, review the mount mode and path guidance below:

items.title: Mount modes
items.text:
Decypharr 2.0+ includes DFS and native Usenet support in stable releases. You no longer need to install the beta branch to use these features.

Choose the mount behavior during onboarding or in Decypharr's DUMB Config. Save DUMB-level changes with Save to File; apply them when it is safe to restart the service.

Geek details: mount configuration example

Choose the mount behavior with mount_type:

{
"decypharr": {
  "mount_type": "dfs",
  "mount_path": "/mnt/debrid/decypharr"
}
}

For a new Decypharr-managed folder, dfs is the recommended default. Built-in rclone is another managed folder option. external_rclone uses a separate DUMB-managed mount, while none is for setups that do not need Decypharr to supply a local folder. Review existing consumers before changing a working mount.

Geek details: mount implementations and provider synchronization Mount Type Description dfs Decypharr File System. Recommended default for Decypharr-managed streaming paths. rclone Embedded rclone managed by Decypharr. DUMB synchronizes Debrid providers from api_keys. external_rclone DUMB-managed external rclone mount pointed at Decypharr WebDAV. none No mount; Decypharr exposes API/WebDAV behavior only. Geek details: mount ownership and configuration reconciliation

When mount_type is rclone, DUMB builds the embedded rclone block and synchronizes debrids entries from the api_keys map. When mount_type is external_rclone, DUMB reconciles the matching managed rclone instance. DFS settings such as mount.dfs.cache_dir are app-owned; DUMB only ensures required startup paths exist and have the configured ownership.

items.title: Native Usenet
items.text:
Add and test your Usenet provider account in Decypharr's Embedded UI. Then open the linked Arr's Embedded UI → Settings → Download Clients and test decypharr-usenet. If you also use Debrid, keep and test the separate Debrid download client. Both can be used by the same Arr.

Geek details: alternative manual SABnzbd-compatible client setup

Decypharr 2.0+ can connect directly to NNTP providers (no Sabnzbd container needed). Configure Usenet inside the Decypharr UI or config.json. DUMB does not manage Usenet provider credentials.

To wire Arrs to Decypharr Usenet manually, add a Sabnzbd download client in Sonarr/Radarr:

  • Host: 127.0.0.1 for an Arr running inside DUMB; use a reachable DUMB address for an external Arr.
  • Port: Decypharr's saved DUMB port, normally 8282.
  • API Key: Decypharr API token (Settings → Auth).
  • Category: the category configured for that Arr instance, normally sonarr or radarr.

DUMB 2.23.0 creates this client with an empty URL Base. Check that generated client before making manual changes.

DUMB creates this Sabnzbd-compatible client automatically for Arr instances whose core_service includes decypharr after Decypharr has Usenet providers configured. You can keep the normal Decypharr qBittorrent-style client for torrents and use the Sabnzbd-style client for NZBs.

Geek details: manual credentials, API pacing and external-container mounts

items.title: Embedded provider keys
items.text:
Use api_keys to define provider credentials:

{
"api_keys": {
  "realdebrid": "rd_...",
  "torbox": "tb_...",
  "alldebrid": "ad_...",
  "debridlink": "dl_..."
}
}

Protect API keys

Debrid API keys grant access to your account. Treat them like secrets.

items.title: TorBox API pacing
items.text:
DUMB uses a conservative starting profile when adding TorBox or filling missing or empty provider settings:

{
  "rate_limit": "2/second",
  "torrents_refresh_interval": "30m"
}

rate_limit paces routine requests at two per second, about 120 per minute sustained. torrents_refresh_interval refreshes the provider torrent catalog every 30 minutes, trading catalog freshness for fewer full-list requests. Download-link refresh and worker settings keep their mount-mode defaults.

Existing nonempty tuning is preserved, including values saved by earlier DUMB versions. Defaults for other providers are unchanged. To apply this profile to an existing TorBox entry, open Decypharr's Service Config tab in the dashboard, find its entry under debrids, and edit only the two fields above. Keep its credentials and other settings, then Save Service Config and restart Decypharr when ready to apply the change. See service configuration editors.

TorBox's current API limits specify a general ceiling of 300 requests per minute separately for each endpoint and API key, with tighter hourly limits for some creation operations. DUMB's profile is a starting point for reducing routine API pressure. Retries, media range requests, and other applications using the same key have their own request behavior and can still encounter limits.

items.title: 1. Bind Mount Setup
items.text:
If you are passing the rclone mount to an external Arr or media server container, include the following bind mounts in both your DUMB and arrs docker-compose files (replace ... with the full host path to your DUMB bind mount):

DUMB ComposeArrs Compose (Sonarr/Radarr) 
volumes:
  - .../DUMB/mnt/debrid:/mnt/debrid:rshared

volumes:
  - .../DUMB/mnt/debrid:/mnt/debrid:rslave

When Required

These mounts are only required when Arrs or media servers run outside the DUMB container and need access to the rclone mount and Decypharr symlinks.

items.title: 2. Configure Root Folders in Arrs
items.text:
When core_service is set to decypharr (or includes it), DUMB automatically creates the root folders and updates the Arr settings for you. If core_service includes Decypharr plus another workflow service such as infinidysk or altmount, the Arr root folder base switches to /mnt/debrid/combined_symlinks/<slug>. Decypharr-only hybrid Debrid+Usenet setups keep the Decypharr root. Manual configuration is only required when core_service is left blank or you want to override the combined workflow wiring.

Inside the Sonarr and Radarr web UI:

  • Navigate to Settings > Media Management > Root Folders

  • Add the following paths:

  • Radarr: /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/{slugged folder name}

  • Sonarr: /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/{slugged folder name}

Required Paths

These directories are managed by Decypharr and must be used for proper operation.

Combined root folder

If core_service includes Decypharr plus another workflow service such as infinidysk or altmount, DUMB switches the base path to /mnt/debrid/combined_symlinks/{slugged folder name} for the Arr root folders. Decypharr-only hybrid Debrid+Usenet setups keep the Decypharr root.

Per-instance folders

For named instances, DUMB uses a slugged folder name like radarr-4k or sonarr-anime. The full paths become /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/radarr-4k and /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/sonarr-anime.

Manual folder naming

If you configure root folders manually, create a matching folder inside /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/ using your preferred naming scheme, then use that folder for both the Arr root folder and your media server library.

items.title: 3. Connect Decypharr to Arrs
items.text:
When core_service is set to decypharr (or includes it), DUMB automatically wires the download client and Arr permissions. If core_service includes Decypharr plus another workflow service such as infinidysk or altmount, Arrs will point at /mnt/debrid/combined_symlinks/<slug> instead of the Decypharr-only root. Manual configuration is only required when core_service is left blank or you want to override the combined workflow wiring.

Follow the official Arr integration guide for current Sonarr and Radarr connection guidance.

Connection Tips

This includes setting the correct API keys and ensuring URL paths match the container environments.

items.title: 4. Media server library setup
items.text:
In your media server (Plex/Jellyfin/Emby), add the same curated folders saved in your Arr root-folder settings. For a Decypharr-only setup these are:

  • Movies Library: /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/{slugged folder name}
  • TV Shows Library: /mnt/debrid/decypharr_symlinks/{slugged folder name}

For combined workflows, use the saved /mnt/debrid/combined_symlinks/<slug> folder instead. Avoid adding the entire provider mount when you want only the organized Arr library.

Library Benefits

This ensures the media server indexes files processed and renamed by Decypharr, enabling clean and consistent playback.

items.title: Troubleshooting Tips
items.text:
For TorBox HTTP 429 responses, check Decypharr's logs for the affected endpoint, retry frequency, and timestamps. Review the saved provider settings and other applications sharing the API key against TorBox's current limits. Persistent stalls need their own request and timeout logs; changing the pacing profile alone does not establish their cause.

Common Issues

  • When using external services, ensure the bind mounts are correct and both containers see the same /mnt/debrid structure
  • Make sure Decypharr has permission to write to and create symlinks in the target directory
  • If media doesn't appear in Plex, check that the symlink folders are scanned and indexed
  • Use docker inspect to verify correct mount propagation between DUMB and Arrs

Permission changes

DUMB updates Arr media-management permissions to enable chmod operations (folder 777, file 666). If you manage permissions manually, review these settings after integration.

items.title: Emby (Core Service)
items.text: Emby is a media server for organizing and streaming your media library. It is a commercial alternative to Plex and Jellyfin.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
Use the same curated library folder in your collector and media server. A running server is only the first check.

flowchart TD
    A["Open Emby and finish sign-in"] --> B
    B["Choose the curated library folder"] --> C
    C["Check the mount before scanning"] --> D
    D["Scan a small library"] --> E
    E["Play and seek through one item"]

items.title: First start
items.text:
1. Select Emby during DUMB onboarding. Open its service card and, on DUMB Config, use Start if stopped. Select Embedded UI to open Emby.
  2. Complete Emby's setup wizard and create the administrator account, or sign in to your existing server. Keep the account credentials for future library and playback changes.
  3. Add a library for each media type and browse to the curated folder used by your download workflow. These are paths inside DUMB, usually below /mnt/debrid, rather than paths from your computer. Use the folder saved in Sonarr/Radarr or your collector's settings.
  4. Review scan and automatic removal settings before scanning a remote library. Confirm the provider mount is available, then run the first library scan.
  5. Open the library, play one item and seek to another point. If it is missing, compare the library folder with the workflow's saved folder; if playback fails, check the provider connection and whether Emby needs transcoding.
  6. Configure remote access, sharing and hardware acceleration after local playback works. Host GPU access and the application's transcoding settings are separate setup steps.

items.title: What Emby provides
items.text:
Endpoint Purpose Default Web UI Emby browser UI http://<host>:8096/

Traefik access

If Traefik is enabled, the Emby UI is proxied at http://<host>:18080/service/ui/emby/; DUMB preserves Emby's internal /web path handling.

Release pinning

When release_version_enabled is set, DUMB treats the release as pinned and disables scheduled auto-updates for Emby.

Technical details: configuration reference

items.title: Configuration in dumb_config.json
items.text:
{
"emby": {
  "enabled": false,
  "process_name": "Emby Media Server",
  "repo_owner": "MediaBrowser",
  "repo_name": "Emby.Releases",
  "release_version_enabled": false,
  "release_version": "4.8.11.0",
  "use_system_ffmpeg": true,
  "suppress_logging": false,
  "log_level": "INFO",
  "port": 8096,
  "auto_update": false,
  "auto_update_interval": 24,
  "auto_update_start_time": "04:00",
  "config_dir": "/emby",
  "config_file": "/emby/config/system.xml",
  "log_file": "/emby/log/embyserver.txt",
  "command": [],
  "env": {}
}
}

items.title: Key configuration fields
items.text:
• port: Web UI port (default 8096).
  • use_system_ffmpeg: Use the system ffmpeg binary when available.
  • release_version_enabled, release_version: Pin to a specific Emby release.
  • auto_update: Enable scheduled update checks (disabled when pinning releases).
  • config_dir, config_file, log_file: Paths for config and logs.

items.title: Accessing the UI
items.text:
Open the service from DUMB's Embedded UI tab when available. The native URLs below require the corresponding Docker host port to be published; use the port saved in your running configuration.

  • Navigate to: http://<host>:8096
  • Traefik proxy: http://<host>:18080/service/ui/emby/
  • With service UIs enabled in DUMB, open Embedded UI on the Emby service page and sign in to Emby there.

See Jellyfin and Emby embedded libraries for login and empty-library troubleshooting.

items.title: Media Library Protection
items.text:
Emby requires a dedicated API key before DUMB can inspect sessions and temporarily control scan tasks/library real-time monitoring. DUMB does not create this key during Emby's first-run administrator setup. Create it in Emby's dashboard, then save it under Library Protection on the Emby service page. Review the configured mount scope and enablement before using protection. Without usable credentials, unattended storage maintenance is deferred because activity is unknown.

See Media Library Protection.

items.title: Health monitoring
items.text:
DUMB checks Emby's /emby/System/Ping endpoint. HTTP 200 with the plain-text reply Emby Server is a successful application ping. When the process and port checks also pass, DUMB displays Healthy.

Health details explain failed or unrecognized responses. The ping confirms server responsiveness; library access, media paths, and playback need their own checks. See health states and application probes.
