items.title: NeutArr
items.text: NeutArr schedules missing-content and upgrade searches in selected Radarr, Sonarr, Lidarr, and Whisparr instances. It is disabled by default. Review targets, schedules, and limits before enabling searches against your indexers.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
NeutArr acts on connected libraries according to your chosen rules. Check exact instances and limits before scheduling work.

flowchart TD
    A["Open NeutArr"] --> B
    B["Connect the intended Arr instances"] --> C
    C["Review searches and limits"] --> D
    D["Enable the intended automation"] --> E
    E["Inspect its activity and Arr queues"]

items.title: First start
items.text:
1. Select NeutArr during onboarding and opt in only the Arr instances you want it to search. For an existing Arr instance, open its DUMB Config, enable use_neutarr and Save to File.
  2. Open the NeutArr service card. On DUMB Config, use Start if stopped, then select Embedded UI.
  3. Review the discovered Arr connections and quality profiles in NeutArr. Do not activate a schedule until the intended applications are connected and unexpected targets are excluded.
  4. Choose conservative search intervals and limits. These searches use your indexers and provider allowances; a running service does not mean you need to enable every search type.
  5. Observe one search cycle in NeutArr and the Arr queue before widening the schedule or adding targets.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
NeutArr integrates with your Arr stack to automate the hunt for:

  • Missing content - Movies, TV episodes, or music not yet downloaded
  • Quality upgrades - Better releases that meet your quality profiles
  • Cutoff unmet - Content below your configured quality cutoff

DUMB supports multiple NeutArr instances, allowing you to run separate hunters for different Arr configurations (e.g., one for Decypharr-linked services and one for InfiniDysk-linked services).

items.title: Service relationships
items.text: Classification Role Core service Automated Arr hunting engine Depends on None Integrates Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr Exposes UI Yes (Web UI)

items.title: Default ports
items.text:
Instance Port Default 9705

Additional NeutArr instances must use unique ports.

items.title: Automation in DUMB
items.text:
Choose the target Arr instances in onboarding or through each Arr's DUMB Config → use_neutarr, then Save to File. DUMB maintains those selected connections; configure the search policy and schedule in NeutArr's Embedded UI.

If you run multiple NeutArr instances, review each one's workflow filter so the same Arr is not searched unintentionally by several schedules.

Geek details: JSON opt-ins, workflow filters and connection storage

DUMB auto-populates NeutArr with Arr instances that opt in.

  1. Set use_neutarr: true on the Arr instances you want NeutArr to manage.
  2. (Optional) Set core_service on the NeutArr instance to filter which Arr instances it pulls in.

Example Arr instance:

{
"radarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Decypharr": {
      "enabled": true,
      "core_service": "decypharr",
      "use_neutarr": true,
      "port": 7878,
      "config_file": "/radarr/decypharr/config.xml"
    }
  }
}
}

Example NeutArr instance filter:

{
"neutarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Decypharr": {
      "core_service": ["decypharr", "infinidysk", "altmount"]
    }
  }
}
}

With that filter in place, the NeutArr instance only receives Arr entries whose core services overlap the NeutArr instance. If core_service is left blank on a NeutArr instance, it can receive all Arr instances with use_neutarr: true. For deeper behavior details, see Core Service Routing.

Auto-configuration storage

DUMB writes NeutArr configuration into NeutArr's JSON config files under the instance config_dir (for example general.json, sonarr.json, radarr.json, and users.json). You can still tune settings in the NeutArr UI, but DUMB will keep the Arr instance list and related config in sync.

Technical details: configuration reference

items.title: Configuration settings in dumb_config.json
items.text:
Below is a sample configuration for NeutArr within the dumb_config.json file:

{
"neutarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Default": {
      "enabled": false,
      "core_service": "",
      "process_name": "NeutArr",
      "repo_owner": "I-am-PUID-0",
      "repo_name": "NeutArr",
      "release_version_enabled": false,
      "release_version": "latest",
      "commit_sha": "",
      "branch_enabled": false,
      "branch": "main",
      "suppress_logging": false,
      "log_level": "INFO",
      "port": 9705,
      "auto_update": false,
      "auto_update_interval": 24,
      "auto_update_start_time": "04:00",
      "clear_on_update": false,
      "exclude_dirs": [
        "/neutarr/default/config"
      ],
      "platforms": [
        "python"
      ],
      "command": [
        "/neutarr/default/venv/bin/python",
        "main.py"
      ],
      "config_dir": "/neutarr/default",
      "config_file": "/neutarr/default/config/general.json",
      "log_file": "/neutarr/default/config/logs/neutarr.log",
      "env": {
        "NEUTARR_CONFIG_DIR": "/neutarr/default/config",
        "NEUTARR_PORT": "{port}"
      }
    }
  }
}
}

items.title: Configuration key descriptions
items.text:
• enabled: Whether to start this NeutArr instance.
  • process_name: Display name used in logs and the frontend.
  • repo_owner / repo_name: GitHub repository to pull from.
  • release_version_enabled / release_version: Use a tagged release if enabled.
  • commit_sha: Build this instance from an exact full 40-character GitHub SHA. It overrides release/branch selection and disables automatic updates for that instance until cleared.
  • branch_enabled / branch: Use a specific branch if enabled.
  • suppress_logging: Suppresses service messages in the main DUMB output.
  • log_level: Logging verbosity (e.g., DEBUG, INFO).
  • port: Port the NeutArr web UI is exposed on.
  • auto_update: Enables DUMB's scheduled update checks; auto_update_mode determines whether a detected update is installed.
  • auto_update_interval: How often (in hours) to check for updates.
  • clear_on_update: Clears build artifacts or cache during updates.
  • exclude_dirs: Prevents specific directories from being affected by updates.
  • platforms: Required runtime (typically python).
  • command: The command used to launch NeutArr.
  • config_dir / config_file: Where configuration files are stored.
  • log_file: Path to the NeutArr log file.
  • env: Environment variables passed at runtime.

items.title: Multi-instance support
items.text:
DUMB supports running multiple NeutArr instances to work with different Arr configurations. The default config ships with a single Default instance.

Instance Use Case Default General use with any Arr instances you opt in Custom instances Separate hunters for different core_service values

Each instance maintains its own:

  • Configuration directory
  • JSON config files
  • Web UI port
  • Log output

items.title: NeutArr web UI
items.text:
Open the service from DUMB's Embedded UI tab when available. The native URLs below require the corresponding Docker host port to be published; use the port saved in your running configuration.

NeutArr provides a web interface for:

  • Configuring which Arr services to monitor
  • Setting search intervals and limits
  • Viewing hunt status and history
  • Manual search triggers

Access the UI at http://<host>:<port> or through the DUMB frontend's embedded service UI feature.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Start with conservative search intervals to avoid rate limiting from indexers.
  • Use separate NeutArr instances when you have Arr services connected to different download clients.
  • Monitor logs via the DUMB frontend or from the log_file path defined for each instance.
  • NeutArr respects your Arr quality profiles, so configure those first.

items.title: Resources
items.text: • NeutArr GitHub Repository

items.title: NzbDAV has moved to InfiniDysk
items.text:
NzbDAV is now InfiniDysk. The project repository, service name, and fresh DUMB defaults have moved to infinidysk/infinidysk.

Use the current InfiniDysk service guide for installation, configuration, troubleshooting, and the complete opt-in migration workflow. Existing DUMB installations continue to support legacy NzbDAV keys, paths, and environment variables until their operator chooses a migration path.

Open the InfiniDysk migration guide

items.title: Plex Media Server (Core Service)
items.text: Plex organizes and streams media from local folders or mounted remote content. DUMB manages its process and persistent data; you choose the Plex account, library paths, sharing policy, and transcoding settings.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
Use the same curated library folder in your collector and media server. A running server is only the first check.

flowchart TD
    A["Open Plex and finish sign-in"] --> B
    B["Choose the curated library folder"] --> C
    C["Check the mount before scanning"] --> D
    D["Scan a small library"] --> E
    E["Play and seek through one item"]

items.title: How to Start
items.text:
1. Select Plex during DUMB onboarding. For a fresh server on the release backend, provide its short-lived claim token immediately before startup.
  2. Open the Plex service card. On DUMB Config, use Start if stopped, then select Embedded UI. Sign in to Plex and confirm your intended account owns this server.
  3. In the Plex setup wizard or server library settings, create a library for each media type. Browse to the curated folder used by your workflow, using the path inside DUMB. For an Arr workflow, compare it with the saved Sonarr/Radarr root folder.
  4. Keep automatic trash removal disabled while validating a remote mount. Confirm that mount is available, then scan the new library.
  5. Open one imported item and test playback and seeking. If it does not appear, compare the saved library path with your workflow's folder; if playback fails, check the provider connection and Plex's stream status.
  6. Set up sharing, remote access or hardware transcoding after local playback works. Account authorization, library access and playback are separate checks.

A Plex claim token authorizes a server claim. A Plex API token lets configured integrations call that server; neither token grants a Plex Pass subscription or its features.

items.title: Utilize the onboarding process
items.text: You can reopen onboarding from Settings → Launch Onboarding. Review account authorization and selected library paths rather than recreating an existing server.

items.title: Manually
items.text:
Technical details: manual Plex startup

For manual configuration, review the plex settings below. A fresh instance needs a valid plex_claim immediately before startup. Start Plex from its DUMB service page. A deliberately published native port also allows http://<host>:32400/web access.

items.title: Service Relationships
items.text: Classification Role Core Service Media Server / Playback Host Depends On Optional None Exposes UI Yes (Web UI on port 32400) Technical details: configuration reference

items.text:
{
"plex": {

  "auto_update_start_time": "04:00",

  "config_file": "/plex/Plex Media Server/Preferences.xml",
  "log_file": "/plex/Plex Media Server/Logs/Plex Media Server.log",
  "plex_claim": "",
  "friendly_name": "DUMB",
  "dbrepair": {
    "enabled": false,

items.title: Key configuration fields
items.text:
• enabled: Toggle Plex Media Server on or off.
  • plex_claim: Plex claim token for initial server registration.
  • friendly_name: The name that appears in the Plex Web App and on local clients.
  • config_dir: Directory containing Plex server data (including preferences).
  • port: Default access port (32400).
  • pinned_version: Pin Plex to a specific version when using manual builds.
  • dbrepair: Optional DBRepair configuration for scheduled Plex database maintenance.

DUMB does not yet support port assignment for Plex Media Server

items.title: Media Library Protection
items.text:
The Plex service page includes Library Protection. Review the configured mount scope and policy. When enabled, DUMB uses its existing Plex token to check sessions, inhibit scans before rclone/InfiniDysk/Decypharr/Zurg/AltMount/CLI Debrid maintenance, and restore Plex after the dependency stabilizes. The same panel exposes live Plex library preferences, including Empty trash automatically after every scan; keep that option off for remote or virtual libraries.

See Media Library Protection for the override choices, recommended Plex settings, recovery journal, and limitations.

items.title: Optional Plex Cloud Status
items.text:
The Plex service page includes a capability-gated Plex Status panel on current DUMB/dmbdb versions. It can enable a cached metric sourced from Plex's official status page, choose a 60-3600 second polling interval, refresh the sample, and show affected components, incidents, or scheduled maintenance without leaving dmbdb.

This option is disabled by default and lives under dumb.metrics.plex_status; it is not a Plex process setting. DUMB makes the public request without a Plex token or local server data. Treat it as cloud-service context only: the local Plex process can be healthy during a Plex cloud incident, and Plex can report all systems operational while a local DUMB, network, remote-access, or playback problem remains.

See Metrics Collection for configuration and failure behavior.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
Plex must have access to:

  • Media directories (local or rclone-mounted).
  • Transcoding cache (if transcoding is enabled).
  • Valid claim token for first-time setup (if not already configured).

items.title: Migrating an Existing Plex Server into DUMB
items.text:
If you're migrating an existing Plex Media Server into the DUMB container, the process involves preserving your current Plex data directory and ensuring it is placed correctly within the DUMB ecosystem.

Preserve the existing server

Back up the complete Plex application data and stop the source server before copying it. Keep the original data until the copied server's ownership, library paths and playback have been checked. Moving application data requires access to the Docker host; the procedure below is for that operator.

Geek details: copy an existing server, adjust paths and verify permissions

items.title: Step 1: Locate your existing Plex data directory
items.text:
Plex keeps its state in a folder named Plex Media Server. That folder contains:

  • Preferences.xml
  • Plug-in Support/Databases/ (library DB)
  • Metadata/, Media/, Cache/, Logs/, and more

Common locations:

Environment Typical Plex data path Linux (native) /var/lib/plexmediaserver/Library/Application Support/Plex Media Server Linux (snap) ~/snap/plexmediaserver/common/Library/Application Support/Plex Media Server Docker Your mapped volume (example: /path/to/plex → /config)

What you need to copy

Copy the entire Plex Media Server folder, not just Preferences.xml.

items.title: Step 2: Copy the Plex data into DUMB
items.text:
Whether your current Plex server is running as a Docker container or directly on the host machine, locate its configuration directory. This directory typically contains:

  • Plex Media Server/Preferences.xml
  • Plex Media Server/Plug-in Support/Databases/...
  • Plex Media Server/Logs/...

Stop Plex before copying

Stop the existing Plex server before copying data to avoid a partial or corrupted database copy.

Copy this entire Plex configuration directory to the DUMB host's Plex directory:

# Replace /path/to/existing/plex with the path from your host or old container
rsync -a "/path/to/existing/plex/Plex Media Server" "/path/to/DUMB/data/plex/"

The result should be:

DUMB/data/plex/Plex Media Server/Preferences.xml
DUMB/data/plex/Plex Media Server/Plug-in Support/Databases/...

The internal path must remain /plex/Plex Media Server/Preferences.xml inside the container, unless you follow Step 3 below.

items.title: Step 3: Point DUMB to the copied config
items.text:
This is only required if changing the default location (shown below) for Plex configs inside the container

Update the dumb_config.json to ensure the config_dir is /plex, which is the internal path mounted inside the container.

{
  "plex": {
    "enabled": true,
    "config_dir": "/plex",
    "config_file": "/plex/Plex Media Server/Preferences.xml"
  }
}

items.title: Step 4: Verify permissions
items.text:
Plex must be able to read and write the copied files. If you see permission errors, adjust ownership to match the user defined in your Docker compose.

Match PUID/PGID ownership

The Plex data directory should be owned by the same UID/GID used in the container (PUID/PGID). Example:

# Replace 1000:1000 with your container PUID:PGID and adjust the path
sudo chown -R 1000:1000 /path/to/DUMB/data/plex
sudo chmod -R u+rwX,g+rwX /path/to/DUMB/data/plex

If your container uses a different PUID/PGID (for example, 568:568 on some NAS setups), use that instead.

items.title: Step 5: Add media content
items.text:
If you have existing media content from your previous Plex setup:

  1. Mount to a custom path (e.g., /mnt/local):

    Custom Path

    Using /mnt/local or any other custom path allows you to preserve legacy media folder structures separately from DUMB's collection system..

    You can also consolidate or symlink these into /mnt/debrid if needed.

    Example Docker Compose snippet:

    volumes:
  - /path/to/old/media/movies:/mnt/local/movies
  - /path/to/old/media/shows:/mnt/local/shows

  2. Update Plex library folders in the Plex Web UI to match the new internal container paths (e.g., /mnt/local/movies).

items.title: Step 6: Restart and verify
items.text:
Once configuration and mounts are complete:

  1. Start the DUMB container.
  2. Access Plex via http://<host>:32400/web.
  3. Verify:
    • Your old libraries and settings are intact
    • Media paths resolve correctly
    • Server is claimed and signed in to Plex.tv

items.title: Optional: reclaim or reconfigure
items.text:
If you're reusing an old server and want to reset it:

  • Delete Preferences.xml to force a new setup
  • Provide a new plex_claim token in dumb_config.json

This allows you to re-register the server cleanly if needed.

items.title: Summary Table
items.text:
Migration Source Steps Plex Docker Container Copy container's volume contents to DUMB/data/plex Plex on Host Copy /var/lib/plexmediaserver or equivalent to DUMB/data/plex Plex Media Bind mount original media directories to /mnt/debrid in DUMB

Once complete, your DUMB-based Plex server should fully replicate your prior setup while gaining the integration benefits of the DUMB ecosystem.

items.title: Hardware Transcoding
items.text:
Hardware-accelerated streaming enables Plex to use the GPU or specialized hardware encoders to offload and speed up transcoding operations, significantly improving performance and lowering CPU usage.

Plex Pass Required

Hardware-accelerated transcoding is a premium feature and requires an active Plex Pass subscription. Learn more

Geek details: prepare Docker GPU access and a writable transcode directory

items.title: Docker Setup for Hardware Transcoding
items.text:
To enable hardware transcoding in a Docker container, pass through the GPU device and provide Plex with a writable transcode directory:

volumes:
  - ./data/plex/transcode:/transcode

devices:
  - /dev/dri:/dev/dri

Create the host directory before starting DUMB and make sure it is writable by the configured PUID:PGID:

mkdir -p ./data/plex/transcode
sudo chown -R 1000:1000 ./data/plex/transcode

Adjust 1000:1000 to match your container PUID and PGID. Without a writable /transcode mount, Plex can log Error creating directory "/transcode": Permission denied and fall back to software transcoding or fail to transcode.

The device mapping grants the container access to the host system's Direct Rendering Infrastructure (DRI), which is required for GPU access (e.g., Intel Quick Sync, NVIDIA NVENC).

items.title: Intel Quick Sync Users
items.text:
Additional permissions may be needed:

group_add:
  - "992"  # Typically 'render' group
  - "993"  # Some systems require both 'render' and 'video'

You can confirm the group IDs for your system by running:

getent group video
getent group render

Make sure the Plex container runs with appropriate PUID and PGID values that also have access to /dev/dri.

items.title: Enabling in Plex Settings
items.text:
Once the container is running and hardware access is configured:

  1. Go to the Plex Web UI: http://<host>:32400/web
  2. Navigate to: Settings > Transcoder
  3. Enable the checkbox: Use hardware acceleration when available
  4. (Optional) Enable Use hardware-accelerated video encoding for encoding tasks.

items.title: Confirming Hardware Transcoding is Active
items.text:
When a video is playing:

  1. Click the three dots next to the playback and choose Stats for Nerds
  2. Look for entries like hw or h264_qsv or nvenc which indicate hardware acceleration.
  3. Alternatively, open the Server Dashboard during playback and check the stream status for an (hw) label next to the transcoding type.
Geek details: inspect GPU use from the container shell

items.title: Monitoring GPU Usage from Inside the Container
items.text: You can supplement Plex's built-in tools (like "Stats for Nerds") with real-time GPU monitoring inside the DUMB container.

items.title: Intel iGPU Monitoring
items.text:
Intel GPUs (e.g., Quick Sync) can be monitored using intel-gpu-tools:

# Enter the container
docker exec -it DUMB bash

# Install the tools (Debian/Ubuntu based images)
apt update && apt install -y intel-gpu-tools

# Launch real-time GPU monitor
intel_gpu_top

This provides a live view of the GPU's video encode/decode engines. Look for activity under:

  • Video or Video/0 for decoding
  • VideoEnhance or Blitter for scaling and filtering

Use q to exit intel_gpu_top

items.title: NVIDIA GPU Monitoring
items.text:
For NVIDIA GPUs with NVENC/NVDEC support, use the nvidia-smi tool:

# Enter the container
docker exec -it DUMB bash

# If not already installed, install NVIDIA tools
apt update && apt install -y nvidia-smi

# Monitor GPU usage
nvidia-smi

Look for the Plex process listed under the Processes section. When active transcoding is occurring, you should see:

  • Increased GPU-Util percentage
  • Encoder usage
  • Memory allocation from Plex or Plex Transcoder

If nvidia-smi is not recognized, ensure the container is running with the --gpus all flag and NVIDIA Docker runtime is enabled on the host.

items.title: Troubleshooting GPU Access & Hardware Transcoding
items.text:
• Confirm the container has access to /dev/dri or sometimes /dev/nvidia*
  • Confirm Plex Pass is active and the account used in Plex is signed in and authorized
  • Validate Plex transcoder settings are enabled for hardware use
  • Check that Plex is actually transcoding (not Direct Playing)
  • Ensure your hardware supports it (Intel iGPU, NVIDIA GPU with driver support, etc.)
  • Review container logs and Plex logs for errors related to transcoding

items.title: Integration with Other Services
items.text:
Plex is designed to serve content collected and maintained by core DUMB services including Riven, CLI Debrid, and Decypharr. These services fetch, organize, and optionally symlink media content into the mounted directory used by Plex.

By default, media content is made available inside the container at /mnt/debrid through rclone mounts.

  • Core services populate /mnt/debrid with downloaded or upgraded content.
  • Plex scans this location to index and serve the media.

If you want to serve media from the host system, bind mount your local media directory into the container and add it as a library path in Plex.

items.title: Access
items.text:
Open the service from DUMB's Embedded UI tab when available. The native URLs below require the corresponding Docker host port to be published; use the port saved in your running configuration.

  • URL: http://<host>:32400/web
  • Credentials: Managed through Plex.tv account

items.title: Mount and Path Planning
items.text:
Ensure your media storage is accessible to Plex via the correct container path.

  • Default internal mount: /mnt/debrid
  • Add bind mounts: for local media stored on the host machine not managed by DUMB.

items.title: Tips and Troubleshooting
items.text:
• If the container fails to start due to permissions, ensure Plex has proper access to its config_dir and media directories.
  • Use PUID and PGID to match host user permissions.
  • Logs can be viewed directly from the DUMB Frontend.
  • You can also start, stop, restart Plex, and modify the dumb_config.json or Plex Preferences.xml from the DUMB Frontend interface.

items.title: Resources
items.text:
• Plex Official Site
  • Plex Claim Token Page
  • Plex Support

items.title: Profilarr
items.text: Profilarr is a profile and custom format manager for Sonarr and Radarr. DUMB supports both the legacy v1 application and the redesigned v2 application, and can auto-link either generation to matching Arr instances.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
Connecting an Arr app and applying profiles are separate actions. Review the selected repository and proposed changes first.

flowchart TD
    A["Open Profilarr"] --> B
    B["Review profile repository"] --> C
    C["Check the intended Sonarr or Radarr connection"] --> D
    D["Select and apply the intended profiles"] --> E
    E["Review the result in the Arr app"]

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Profilarr provides:

  • Repository‑backed profiles - version‑control your profiles and formats
  • Cross‑stack consistency - keep Sonarr/Radarr aligned across debrid and usenet stacks
  • Media management sync - naming rules, quality definitions, and misc settings
  • Version-aware installation - run a v1 release, a v2 release, a branch, or an exact commit
  • Safe v2 ownership - DUMB changes only v2 Arr connections tagged dumb:auto

items.title: Default port
items.text: Service Port Profilarr 6868 Technical details: configuration reference

items.title: Profilarr instance configuration
items.text:
{
"profilarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Default": {
      "enabled": false,
      "core_service": "",
      "process_name": "Profilarr",
      "repo_owner": "Dictionarry-Hub",
      "repo_name": "profilarr",
      "release_version_enabled": false,
      "release_version": "latest",
      "commit_sha": "",
      "branch_enabled": false,
      "branch": "main",
      "suppress_logging": false,
      "log_level": "INFO",
      "port": 6868,
      "auto_update": false,
      "auto_update_interval": 24,
      "auto_update_start_time": "04:00",
      "clear_on_update": true,
      "exclude_dirs": ["/profilarr/default/config"],
      "config_dir": "/profilarr/default",
      "log_file": "/profilarr/default/config/log/profilarr.log"
    }
  }
}
}

items.title: Profilarr instance keys
items.text:
• enabled: Whether to start this Profilarr instance.
  • core_service: Filters which Arr instances are auto‑linked (see below).
  • repo_owner / repo_name: GitHub repository for Profilarr itself.
  • release_version_enabled / release_version: Profilarr is unpinned by default and follows the latest stable release. Enable release pinning and enter an explicit tag such as v1.1.4, v1.1.5, or v2.0.9 to stay on that release.
  • commit_sha: Build this Profilarr instance from an exact full 40-character GitHub SHA. It overrides release/branch selection and disables automatic updates for that instance until cleared.
  • branch_enabled / branch: Use a specific branch if enabled.
  • port: Port the Profilarr UI is exposed on.
  • auto_update / auto_update_interval / auto_update_start_time: Automatic update settings.
  • config_dir / log_file: Profilarr installation/config root and log path.

command, build platforms, and generation-specific environment variables are runtime-managed. DUMB detects the downloaded source layout and writes the correct v1 Gunicorn or v2 standalone command automatically.

items.title: Choosing v1 or v2
items.text:
New configurations default to release_version_enabled: false with release_version: latest, so they follow the current stable Profilarr release without being pinned. Existing DUMB configurations pinned to v1.1.4 remain pinned and continue using the v1 Python/React build.

Selector DUMB behavior Default unpinned selection (release_version_enabled: false) Follows the latest stable release, currently a v2 Deno/SvelteKit build. An explicit v2.x tag Pins and runs the selected v2 Deno/SvelteKit application. A v1.x tag Builds and runs the legacy Python/React application. branch_enabled: true Downloads the selected branch and detects its layout. commit_sha Downloads the exact commit and detects its layout; automatic updates are disabled.

After choosing an explicit release, branch, or commit, use Install configured release/branch/commit or restart the service. For the default unpinned configuration, use the normal update action or restart the service so DUMB resolves and installs the current stable release.

v2 is a fresh application state

Profilarr v2 does not provide an in-place migration from v1 app data. DUMB preserves the shared config root during upgrades, but keeps the primary databases separate: v1 uses config/profilarr.db, while v2 uses config/data/profilarr.db. Configure v2 through its first-run setup instead of expecting v1 users, repositories, or profile selections to be imported.

items.title: Arr instance options
items.text:
Open the intended Sonarr/Radarr instance's DUMB Config, enable use_profilarr and Save to File. Choose a matching workflow filter in Profilarr's DUMB settings. Open Profilarr's Embedded UI to review the connection and choose the profiles, formats and sync behavior you actually want; a linked application is not a complete profile policy.

Geek details: per-instance JSON opt-in

Profilarr linking is controlled per Arr instance:

{
"sonarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Default": {
      "enabled": true,
      "use_profilarr": true
    }
  }
}
}

Key:

  • use_profilarr: Opt this Arr instance into Profilarr linking.

items.title: Auto-linking behavior
items.text:
DUMB automatically links Profilarr to Sonarr/Radarr instances that:

  • are enabled
  • have use_profilarr: true
  • match the Profilarr instance core_service filter

On v1, DUMB retains its original repository seeding and one-time initial-sync behavior. On v2, DUMB creates and updates only Arr connection rows tagged dumb:auto. It deliberately leaves v2 databases, profiles, quality profiles, custom formats, and sync choices under Profilarr's control. A user-created v2 Arr connection with the same name is left unchanged.

items.title: core_service filtering
items.text:
• Blank (""): Manual mode. DUMB does not auto‑link any Arr instances.
  • Single core service (e.g., decypharr): Links only Arrs in that stack.
  • Combined (e.g., decypharr, infinidysk, altmount): Links Arrs across matching Debrid and Usenet stacks.

items.title: v1 default repository seeding
items.text:
This section applies only to Profilarr v1. If no repository is connected, DUMB seeds a default repo on first run:

  • https://github.com/johman10/profilarr-trash-guides

This provides ready‑to‑sync profiles, custom formats, regex patterns, and media management defaults.

items.title: v1 initial sync behavior
items.text:
This section applies only to Profilarr v1. When DUMB creates a new Profilarr app entry, it triggers a one-time initial sync:

  • Profiles
  • Custom formats
  • Regex patterns (used during profile/format compilation)
  • Media management:
  • naming rules
  • misc settings
  • quality definitions

Regex patterns

Regex patterns are not Arr settings. They are used by Profilarr to compile profiles and formats, so they won’t appear in Arr UI.

items.title: Forcing the initial sync again
items.text: Delete the Arr entry in Profilarr and restart Profilarr from the DUMB frontend. DUMB will recreate the entry and run the initial sync again.

items.title: Profilarr v2 notes
items.text:
• Complete Profilarr's account setup when you first open v2.
  • Profilarr v2 initializes its own application database and default Dictionarry v2 database.
  • DUMB retries Arr auto-linking after Profilarr starts so the v2 migrations can finish first.
  • The optional upstream parser service used for custom-format and quality-profile expression testing is not managed by DUMB. Core v2 profile management and Arr synchronization do not require it.
  • v2 supports Linux AMD64 and ARM64 builds in DUMB.

items.title: v1 tagging rules for repo items
items.text:
DUMB uses filename tags to avoid cross‑syncing:

  • Profiles / custom formats require sonarr or radarr in the filename.
  • Regex patterns / media management apply to both if no app‑specific tag is found.

items.title: Missing API keys
items.text:
If auto‑link runs before Arrs finish writing config.xml, you may see:

Profilarr auto-link: missing API key for sonarr ...

DUMB retries automatically after Arr start, but you can also restart Profilarr once the Arrs are fully up.

items.title: Resources
items.text:
• Profilarr Repository
  • Profilarr Docs

items.title: Prowlarr (Core Service)
items.text: Prowlarr is an indexer manager for the Arr ecosystem. It centralizes indexer configuration and syncs them to Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and Whisparr.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
Prowlarr supplies indexer settings to the Arr apps you connect; the download workflow is configured separately.

flowchart TD
    A["Add an indexer in Prowlarr"] --> B
    B["Test its connection"] --> C
    C["Connect the intended Arr apps"] --> D
    D["Review the sync result in each Arr"] --> E
    E["Test a search from the Arr app"]

items.title: First start
items.text:
1. Enable Prowlarr during onboarding, then open its embedded UI.
  2. Add the indexers you intend to use and run their connection tests.
  3. Review the Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, or Whisparr application connections and choose the intended synchronization policy.
  4. Check indexer tags and supported categories so each application receives the sources you expect.

A saved connection is not a passed indexer test. Check both before enabling automated searches.

items.title: Service Relationships
items.text: Classification Role Core Service Indexer manager Depends On None Optional Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Whisparr Exposes UI Yes (Web UI) Technical details: configuration reference

items.title: Configuration in dumb_config.json
items.text:
{
"prowlarr": {
  "instances": {
    "Default": {
      "enabled": false,
      "postgres_enabled": false,
      "postgres_main_db": "",
      "postgres_log_db": "",
      "process_name": "Prowlarr",
      "repo_owner": "Prowlarr",
      "repo_name": "Prowlarr",
      "release_version_enabled": false,
      "release_version": "latest",
      "clear_on_update": false,
      "exclude_dirs": [],
      "platforms": [],
      "suppress_logging": false,
      "auto_update": false,
      "auto_update_interval": 24,
      "auto_update_start_time": "04:00",
      "pinned_version": "",
      "port": 9696,
      "config_dir": "/prowlarr/default",
      "config_file": "/prowlarr/default/config.xml",
      "log_file": "/prowlarr/default/logs/prowlarr.txt",
      "command": [],
      "env": {}
    }
  }
}
}

items.title: Key configuration fields
items.text:
• postgres_enabled: Opt this instance into DUMB-managed PostgreSQL config. SQLite is the default; set this to true only when you want Prowlarr to use PostgreSQL.
  • postgres_main_db / postgres_log_db: Optional database-name overrides. When blank, DUMB uses prowlarr-main and prowlarr-log for the default instance, or unique instance-scoped names for additional instances.
  • port: Web UI port (default 9696).
  • pinned_version: Optional version pin for Prowlarr updates.
  • repo_owner / repo_name: GitHub repo used for releases or branch builds.
  • release_version_enabled / release_version: Use GitHub releases (e.g., latest, nightly, prerelease, or a tag).
  • clear_on_update: Clear the install directory before updating.
  • exclude_dirs: Directories to preserve when clearing.
  • platforms: Build platforms (defaults to ["dotnet"] when using branches).
  • config_dir, config_file, log_file: Paths for config and logs.

items.title: PostgreSQL database mode
items.text:
When postgres_enabled is true, DUMB:

  • enables the bundled PostgreSQL service if needed;
  • creates the Prowlarr main/log databases in postgres.databases;
  • starts PostgreSQL before Prowlarr; and
  • writes the required PostgresUser, PostgresPassword, PostgresHost, PostgresPort, PostgresMainDb, and PostgresLogDb entries to Prowlarr's config.xml.

During onboarding, enabling postgres_enabled for Prowlarr is enough; you do not need to separately select PostgreSQL as an optional service.

This does not migrate existing SQLite data

Setting postgres_enabled: true changes the database backend Prowlarr starts with. It does not copy prowlarr.db into PostgreSQL.

If you enable this on an existing SQLite-backed Prowlarr instance without doing a manual migration, Prowlarr can start against fresh PostgreSQL databases and appear empty or newly initialized.

For an existing instance, use Database Migration on the service page. DUMB requires a rehearsal, initializes an isolated Prowlarr-owned PostgreSQL schema, imports and validates every table, and preserves SQLite for rollback. Prowlarr's upstream guide still classifies migration as unsupported. See SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration.

PostgreSQL is not a temporary toggle

There is no known supported migration path from PostgreSQL back to SQLite for Prowlarr. Treat postgres_enabled: true as a long-term database choice unless you are willing to recreate the Prowlarr instance from scratch.

DUMB can restore the preserved pre-cutover SQLite state, but it does not copy later PostgreSQL writes back into SQLite.

items.title: Repo-based installs and updates
items.text:
Prowlarr now supports the same repository-based controls as other DUMB services.

  • GitHub releases: Set release_version_enabled: true with a valid repo_owner/repo_name.
  • Default updater: Leave release_version_enabled: false to use the standard Arr updater.

GitHub sources take priority when enabled and are not a fallback. pinned_version only applies to the traditional Arr updater.

items.title: Integration with DUMB
items.text:
• Connect Prowlarr to Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr/Whisparr via their API keys and base URLs.
  • Prowlarr can share indexers across all Arr instances to keep setups consistent.

items.title: AIOStreams search integration
items.text:
AIOStreams can query a DUMB-managed Prowlarr instance for torrent and Usenet results:

  1. Copy Prowlarr's API key from Settings → General.
  2. In AIOStreams' built-in Prowlarr settings, enter http://127.0.0.1:9696, replacing 9696 with this instance's saved DUMB port.
  3. Enter the API key and choose the indexers AIOStreams may query.
  4. Add the built-in Prowlarr addon to the configuration on /stremio/configure.

This is an AIOStreams runtime integration, not a Prowlarr application entry that DUMB creates automatically. Prowlarr redirects NZB grabs rather than proxying them, so review indexer rules if searches and grabs can leave through different public IP addresses.

items.title: Automated Arr sync
items.text:
DUMB reads Arr API keys after initialization and can create managed Prowlarr applications. Review the resulting application targets and synchronization policy, and test connections separately from saving entries.

DUMB 2.23.0 synchronizes enabled Arr applications broadly. Review those entries in Prowlarr before relying on automatic indexer synchronization.

Requirements:

  • Prowlarr instance is enabled.
  • Arr instances are enabled with a valid port and readable config_file.
  • Prowlarr API key is available in its config_file.

items.title: Core-service tags
items.text:
DUMB tags Prowlarr application entries when the Arr instance has core_service set (single value or list):

Arr core service Tag applied in Prowlarr decypharr decypharr infinidysk infinidysk altmount altmount

These tags are created automatically if they do not exist.

items.title: Indexer routing via tags
items.text:
Prowlarr uses tags to decide which indexers sync into which Arr apps. DUMB links each Arr app to workflow tags derived from its selected provider links. Review effective categories and indexer tags for the installed Prowlarr version; a tag name alone is not proof that traffic or results are isolated.

When you add custom indexers in Prowlarr, make sure the correct tag is applied so they sync to the intended Arr apps.

items.title: Custom indexer sync (Decypharr)
items.text:
When Decypharr is enabled, DUMB also syncs custom indexer definitions and creates indexers:

  • Zilean (Torznab) with a base URL that prefers the local Zilean instance when enabled, and defaults to https://zileanfortheweebs.midnightignite.me otherwise. You can override the URL in Prowlarr after it is created.
  • StremThru (Torznab) using the hosted endpoint

If Decypharr is enabled, DUMB automatically enables the public StremThru indexer.

For Whisparr applications, DUMB widens Prowlarr sync categories to include the Movie/TV roots used by the Zilean/StremThru custom definitions plus the common XXX categories. This permits those custom indexers to sync to Whisparr with its selected workflow tags. Validate effective routing with the installed Prowlarr version and your indexer categories; tag names alone do not establish isolation.

Custom definitions are pulled from the Prowlarr-Indexers repository and stored in <prowlarr_config_dir>/Definitions/Custom (or <prowlarr_config_dir>/indexer/Definitions/Custom when present).

Other custom indexers in the definition repository are available to add manually in Prowlarr.

items.title: Accessing the UI
items.text:
Open the service from DUMB's Embedded UI tab when available. The native URLs below require the corresponding Docker host port to be published; use the port saved in your running configuration.

  • Navigate to: http://<host>:9696

items.title: Installation troubleshooting
items.text:
Before extracting an Arr archive, DUMB validates that tar can read the full gzip archive and logs both the downloaded archive size and free space in the installation filesystem. If validation or extraction fails, the structured DUMB error includes tar's stderr, its exit status, the archive size, and the available space. Messages such as unexpected end of file, No space left on device, Permission denied, or Read-only file system therefore remain visible even when /opt/prowlarr is ephemeral.

A Prowlarr preinstall failure no longer shuts down the DUMB API or Frontend. DUMB records the failure, completes the remaining preinstall work, and retries Prowlarr during normal service startup. If the retry also fails, Prowlarr stays stopped while the DUMB control plane remains available for logs and service management.

For repeated extraction failures, check the Docker host's storage and inode capacity at its Docker root directory. A full container removal/recreation deletes the failed archive under /opt, so preserve the complete DUMB log when requesting support.

If extraction reports Function not implemented, the archive and available space are not normally the cause. Ubuntu 26.04's security-hardened GNU tar uses the Linux openat2 interface to confine archive extraction. Older host kernels, container runtimes, or seccomp profiles can return ENOSYS for that interface even when the same installation worked with an older DUMB image. DUMB retries these failures with Python's security-filtered archive extractor, which rejects paths and links that escape /opt/prowlarr.

If both extractors fail, check the host's kernel, Docker, containerd, runc, and seccomp versions. Do not permanently disable seccomp as a workaround; updating the host runtime retains its security boundary and native GNU tar extraction.

items.title: Radarr (Core Service)
items.text: Radarr is a movie manager that automates searching, grabbing, and organizing movies through indexers and download clients.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
Test the connections before adding more requests. The saved root folder must also be visible to your media server.

flowchart TD
    A["Open the app from its service page"] --> B
    B["Test indexers and download client"] --> C
    C["Choose the movie root folder and profile"] --> D
    D["Add one intended item and follow import"] --> E
    E["Scan and play it in the media server"]

items.title: First start
items.text:
1. Select Radarr and its download workflow in DUMB onboarding. Reopen onboarding from Settings → Launch Onboarding if needed.
  2. Open the Radarr service card. On DUMB Config, use Start if stopped, then select Embedded UI. Complete the application's login setup if prompted.
  3. Open Settings → Download Clients and test the client DUMB created for your selected workflow. Under Settings → Indexers, test an indexer added directly or synced from Prowlarr. Both connections must work to find and acquire media.
  4. Review Settings → Media Management → Root Folders. Choose the curated movie library folder for your workflow and use that same folder in your media server. Review Settings → Profiles to choose the quality you want.
  5. Add one intended movie, select that root folder and quality profile, and choose what to monitor. Check Activity → Queue while it is acquired and imported; check Activity → History if it fails.
  6. Scan your media-server library and play the imported item. Finish this test before adding a large library or enabling broad automated searches.

Keep the default SQLite database unless you are planning the separate migration below. The Decypharr, InfiniDysk and AltMount guides explain their different library folders.

items.title: Key configuration fields
items.text:
• core_service: Set to decypharr, infinidysk, altmount, or a list of workflow keys to enable DUMB integration.
  • use_neutarr: Opt this instance into NeutArr automation.
  • use_profilarr: Opt this instance into Profilarr linking.
  • postgres_enabled: Opt this instance into DUMB-managed PostgreSQL config. SQLite is the default; set this to true only when you want Radarr to use PostgreSQL.
  • postgres_main_db / postgres_log_db: Optional database-name overrides. When blank, DUMB uses radarr-main and radarr-log for the default instance, or unique instance-scoped names for additional instances.
  • port: Web UI port (default 7878).
  • pinned_version: Optional version pin for Radarr updates.
  • repo_owner / repo_name: GitHub repo used for releases or branch builds.
  • release_version_enabled / release_version: Use GitHub releases (e.g., latest, nightly, prerelease, or a tag).
  • clear_on_update: Clear the install directory before updating.
  • exclude_dirs: Directories to preserve when clearing.
  • platforms: Build platforms (defaults to ["dotnet"] when using branches).
  • config_dir, config_file, log_file: Paths for config and logs.

items.title: PostgreSQL database mode
items.text:
SQLite is the default and needs no separate setup. If you want to move an existing Radarr instance to PostgreSQL, use Database Migration on its service page. Run a rehearsal, review the validation results, then use guarded cutover. Read the migration guide and back up the instance before proceeding.

Geek details: how PostgreSQL settings and startup are generated

When postgres_enabled is true, DUMB:

  • enables the bundled PostgreSQL service if needed;
  • creates the Radarr main/log databases in postgres.databases;
  • starts PostgreSQL before Radarr; and
  • writes the required PostgresUser, PostgresPassword, PostgresHost, PostgresPort, PostgresMainDb, and PostgresLogDb entries to Radarr's config.xml.

During onboarding, enabling postgres_enabled for Radarr is enough; you do not need to separately select PostgreSQL as an optional service.

This does not migrate existing SQLite data

Setting postgres_enabled: true changes the database backend Radarr starts with. It does not copy radarr.db into PostgreSQL.

If you enable this on an existing SQLite-backed Radarr instance without doing a manual migration, Radarr can start against fresh PostgreSQL databases and appear empty or newly initialized.

For an existing instance, use the Database Migration tool on its service page. Run a rehearsal first, review its table-count validation, and only then start guarded cutover. See SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration.

Radarr's upstream documentation still classifies existing SQLite migration as unsupported. Back up Radarr's /data/radarr persistence and PostgreSQL's /data/postgres persistence (internal paths /radarr/... and /postgres_data) before proceeding, even when using DUMB's guarded workflow.

PostgreSQL is not a temporary toggle

There is no known supported migration path from PostgreSQL back to SQLite for Radarr. Treat postgres_enabled: true as a long-term database choice unless you are willing to recreate the Radarr instance from scratch.

DUMB preserves the pre-cutover SQLite database and can restore its configuration, but it does not copy later PostgreSQL changes back into SQLite.

items.title: Repo-based installs and updates
items.text:
Radarr now supports the same repository-based controls as other DUMB services.

  • GitHub releases: Set release_version_enabled: true with a valid repo_owner/repo_name.
  • Default updater: Leave release_version_enabled: false to use the standard Arr updater.

GitHub sources take priority when enabled and are not a fallback. pinned_version only applies to the traditional Arr updater.

items.title: Integration with DUMB
items.text:
• For Decypharr integration, set core_service to decypharr and follow the Decypharr guide.
  • For InfiniDysk integration, set core_service to infinidysk and follow the InfiniDysk guide.
  • For AltMount integration, set core_service to altmount and follow the AltMount guide.
  • For combined workflows, set core_service to a list such as ["decypharr", "infinidysk", "altmount"].
  • Use Prowlarr to centrally manage indexers and sync them to Radarr.
  • DUMB enables Arr folder permission updates and applies permissions to configured root folders during integration.
  • See Core Service Routing for how core_service affects automation.

items.title: Riven Backend Configuration
items.text: Riven collects media from your chosen lists and requests, then organizes it for your media server. DUMB starts the supporting services; Riven Frontend is where you choose accounts, sources, scrapers and library behavior.

items.title: Initial Setup: Riven Backend
items.text:
1. Select Riven Backend and Riven Frontend in DUMB onboarding, along with your provider and media server. Reopen onboarding from Settings → Launch Onboarding when needed.
  2. Open the Riven Backend service card and check that it is running. Use DUMB Config → Start if stopped and wait for its supporting services to become ready.
  3. Open the Riven Frontend service card, start it if needed, then select Embedded UI → Settings.
  4. Configure your provider account and library paths. Enable at least one Content source so Riven knows what to collect, and at least one suitable Scraper so it can find sources. Review Ranking before importing a large list.
  5. Under Media Server, review the connection to Plex, Jellyfin or Emby and deliberately choose whether its updater should run. Saving a connection alone does not enable that updater.
  6. Add one intended request through the source you enabled. Follow its progress in Riven, check the media-server library, and play the result before enabling broad acquisition.

Required configuration

Installing Riven is only the first step. An account, usable content source, scraper and matching library paths are needed for a working collection workflow.

items.title: Recommended Setup Areas
items.text:
• General – Adjust base settings like min/max files size, etc.
  • Media Server – Review your Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby connection, then choose whether its updater should run.
  • Content – Configure sources such as Trakt, Seerr, or the Plex Watchlist, MDB List, Listrr.
  • Scrapers – Enable one or more scrapers (e.g., Zilean, Torrentio, Knightcrawler, Orionoid, Jackett, Mediafusion, Prowlarr, Comet).
  • Ranking – Customize how results are scored and filtered.

After Configuration

Once complete, Riven will begin processing requests based on the selected sources and configurations.

items.title: Workflow diagram
items.text:
Configure Riven in Riven Frontend. Choose content, scrapers and updater behavior explicitly, then test one request. Geek details: how requests, providers, mounts and libraries connect 
%%{ init: { "flowchart": { "curve": "basis" } } }%%
flowchart TD
    A([Request sources:<br/>Seerr, Trakt,<br/>Plex Watchlist])
    B[[Prowlarr / Indexers]]
    C[Riven]
    D@{shape: cloud, label: "Debrid Providers"}
    E[Zurg or Decypharr<br/>WebDAV]
    F[(Rclone WebDAV Mount<br/>Root Path:<br/>/mnt/debrid/riven)]
    G[Rename + Link Step:<br/>Symlinks]
    H[(Final Symlink Root:<br/>/mnt/debrid/riven_symlinks)]
    I([Media Servers:<br/>Plex, Jellyfin, Emby])

    A <==> C
    B <==> C
    C <==> D

    G ==> H
    F ===> C

    E e3@=== F

    class e1,e2,e3,e4 animate

Port conflicts and auto-shift

Riven defaults (3000/8080) overlap with InfiniDysk defaults. DUMB can auto-shift conflicting ports at container startup or during the onboarding core-service start flow, updating dumb_config.json accordingly. Per-service stop/start/restart does not re-run port conflict resolution, so fix conflicts manually before restarting a single service.

Technical details: configuration reference

items.title: Configuration Key Descriptions
items.text:
• enabled: Whether to start the Riven Backend service.
  • process_name: Used in logs and process tracking.
  • host: IP address for the backend to listen on.
  • port: Port exposed for the API.
  • repo_owner / repo_name: GitHub repo to pull from.
  • release_version_enabled / release_version: Use a tagged release if enabled.
  • commit_sha: Builds an exact Riven revision from its full 40-character GitHub SHA.
  • branch_enabled / branch: Use a specific branch if enabled.
  • suppress_logging: Suppresses service messages in the main DUMB output.
  • log_level: Logging verbosity level (e.g., DEBUG, INFO).
  • auto_update: Enables DUMB's scheduled update checks; auto_update_mode determines whether a detected update is installed.
  • auto_update_interval: How often (in hours) to check for updates.
  • symlink_library_path: Target path for media symlinks.
  • clear_on_update: Clears build artifacts or cache during updates.
  • exclude_dirs: Prevents specific directories from being affected by updates when using clear_on_update
  • env_copy: Copies a .env file from one location to another. Such as the Riven .env discussed below
  • platforms: Expected runtime environment (e.g., python).
  • command: How the service is started.
  • config_dir / config_file: Configuration directory and settings file.
  • log_file: Path to the Riven backend log file.
  • env: Dictionary of environment variables passed to the process.
  • wait_for_dir: Delays startup until the specified directory exists.

items.title: Service updates
items.text:
Review update settings on DUMB Config, then Save to File. Read the update guide before changing a working installation's source or enabling automatic installation.

Geek details: alternative release, branch and exact-commit targets Geek details: environment overrides and maintenance operations

items.title: Commit / Branch / Version Targeting
items.text: Choose a full commit_sha, a release selector, or an enabled branch in this service's DUMB settings. A commit pin takes precedence over the other selectors and disables automatic updates until you clear it. Review source selection and update modes before changing a running service.

items.title: Riven's Environment Variables in the .env.example
items.text:
The .env.example file includes:

  • RIVEN_FORCE_ENV: Forces env vars to override settings.json.
  • SETTINGS_FILENAME: Specifies the settings file name.
  • SKIP_TRAKT_CACHE: Skips cached results.
  • HARD_RESET: Drops and recreates all database tables.
  • REPAIR_SYMLINKS: Fixes any broken symlinks.
  • API_KEY: Custom static API key.
  • WORKERS: Number of indexing workers.

Each Riven env can also be set within DUMB, either through the "env" section of the "riven_backend" within the dumb_config.json, or by using the methods defined in the Configuration section of the docs.

View full example on GitHub

items.title: Seerr
items.text: Seerr (Overseerr/Jellyseerr) is a media request and discovery platform that integrates with Plex, Jellyfin, Radarr, and Sonarr. It allows users to browse, request, and track media content through an intuitive web interface.

items.title: Initial setup
items.text:
After enabling Seerr and starting the service:

  1. Access the Seerr UI at http://<host>:5055
  2. Complete the setup wizard:
  3. Sign in with your Plex account (or configure Jellyfin)
  4. Connect to your Plex/Jellyfin server

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Seerr provides:

  • Media discovery - Browse trending, popular, and upcoming content
  • Request management - Users can request movies and TV shows
  • Integration with Arr services - Automatically sends requests to Radarr/Sonarr
  • User management - Multiple users with different permission levels

items.title: Seerr instance keys
items.text:
• enabled: Whether to start this Seerr instance.

  • postgres_database: Optional database-name override. Blank uses a per-instance DUMB default.
  • sync_role: disabled, primary, or subordinate.

No core_service routing for Seerr

Configure Seerr request routing by selecting the intended Sonarr/Radarr connections, profiles, and roots in Seerr. Seerr Sync is controlled by sync_role plus the top-level seerr_sync block. The low-level core_service field is not used for Decypharr/InfiniDysk/AltMount workflow routing on Seerr and is intentionally hidden from onboarding options.

  • process_name: Display name used in logs and the frontend.
  • repo_owner / repo_name: GitHub repository to pull from.
  • release_version_enabled / release_version: Use a tagged release if enabled.
  • commit_sha: Build this Seerr instance from an exact full 40-character GitHub SHA. It overrides release/branch selection and disables automatic updates for that instance until cleared.
  • branch_enabled / branch: Use a specific branch if enabled.
  • suppress_logging: Suppresses service messages in the main DUMB output.
  • log_level: Logging verbosity (e.g., debug, info, warn).
  • port: Port the Seerr web UI is exposed on.
  • auto_update: Enables DUMB's scheduled update checks; auto_update_mode determines whether a detected update is installed.
  • auto_update_interval: How often (in hours) to check for updates.
  • clear_on_update: Clears build artifacts or cache during updates.
  • exclude_dirs: Prevents specific directories from being affected by updates.
  • platforms: Required runtime (typically pnpm).
  • command: The command used to launch Seerr.
  • config_dir / config_file: Where configuration files are stored.
  • log_file: Path to the Seerr log file.
  • env: Environment variables passed at runtime.

items.title: PostgreSQL migration
items.text:
Each Seerr instance can migrate its /config/db/db.sqlite3 data independently. Open Database Migration on that instance's service page, complete rehearsal, review users/media/requests and full table-count validation, then cut over. DUMB lets Seerr initialize its own current PostgreSQL schema and does not copy Seerr's migration bookkeeping table.

Setting postgres_enabled: true directly does not copy SQLite data. The preserved SQLite database can be restored, but writes made after PostgreSQL cutover are not merged back. See SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration and Seerr database configuration.

items.title: Seerr Sync
items.text:
Seerr Sync replicates requests from one primary Seerr instance to one or more subordinates. It is one‑way and is designed for multi‑Seerr setups where the primary is the source of truth.

For a full overview and use‑case narrative, see Seerr Sync.

items.title: High-level overview
items.text:
Seerr Sync keeps multiple Seerr instances aligned by periodically polling the primary and applying changes to subordinates.

How it works:

  • Polling - Periodically polls the primary for all requests (default 60s).
  • Fingerprinting - Each request is identified by {mediaType}:{tmdbId}:{is4k}.
  • Sync actions - New requests are created on subordinates, status changes propagate, and deletions are optionally mirrored.
  • State persistence - Tracks synced requests in /config/seerr_sync_state.json so it survives restarts.
  • Failure handling - Failed sync attempts are tracked separately and retried after a configurable delay.

Use case example:

Multiple Seerr instances (for example, one per household) can share the same request library. Users submit requests on the primary and they appear on all subordinates, each tied to its own Arr stack.

items.title: Top-level seerr_sync settings
Seerr Sync keys
items.text:
• seerr_sync.enabled: Master toggle for Seerr Sync.
  • seerr_sync.poll_interval_seconds: Poll interval in seconds (minimum 10).
  • seerr_sync.external_primary.enabled: Use an external Seerr as primary.
  • seerr_sync.external_primary.url: External primary base URL.
  • seerr_sync.external_primary.api_key: API key for external primary.
  • seerr_sync.external_subordinates: List of external subordinate URLs + API keys.
  • seerr_sync.options.sync_pending: Sync pending requests.
  • seerr_sync.options.sync_approved: Sync approved requests.
  • seerr_sync.options.sync_declined: Sync declined requests.
  • seerr_sync.options.sync_deletes: Delete subordinates when deleted on primary.
  • seerr_sync.options.sync_4k_separately: Treat 4K as separate requests.
  • seerr_sync.options.user_mapping: Owner mapping (admin or email_match).

Key fields:

  • enabled: Master toggle for Seerr Sync.
  • poll_interval_seconds: Minimum 10 seconds. How often to poll the primary.
  • external_primary: Use an external Seerr as primary (URL + API key required).
  • external_subordinates: External subordinate list (URL + API key required for each).
  • options: Toggles for request types and ownership mapping.

items.title: Per-instance sync_role
items.text:
Each Seerr instance has a sync role:

{
"seerr": {
  "instances": {
    "Default": {
      "enabled": true,
      "sync_role": "disabled"
    }
  }
}
}

Values:

  • disabled: Not part of sync.
  • primary: Source of truth.
  • subordinate: Receives replicated requests.

Validation rules

  • Only one internal primary is allowed.
  • If an external primary is enabled, no internal instance can be primary.
  • A primary must exist (internal or external).
  • At least one subordinate must exist (internal or external).
  • External entries require both URL and API key.

items.title: Frontend integration
items.text:
The Seerr service page includes a Seerr Sync panel with:

  • Enable toggle and polling interval
  • External primary + subordinates editor (API keys are hidden by default)
  • Test buttons to validate external primary and subordinate connectivity
  • Sync options toggles and user mapping
  • Per-instance sync role selector
  • Status + failed request reporting (with clear actions and scrollable list)

items.title: Plex configuration
items.text:
Seerr can sync with your Plex server to:

  • Show what content you already have
  • Display watch status
  • Allow Plex user authentication

items.title: Jellyfin configuration
items.text:
For Jellyfin users, Seerr (Jellyseerr variant) provides similar functionality:

  • Library synchronization
  • User authentication via Jellyfin

items.text:
Configure Radarr and Sonarr in Seerr settings:

Setting Description Hostname 127.0.0.1 (internal to DUMB container) Port Radarr: 7878, Sonarr: 8989 API Key Found in Arr service Settings General Quality Profile Select default quality for requests Root Folder Default download location

Multiple Arr instances

If you have multiple Radarr or Sonarr instances (e.g., for 4K content), you can add them all to Seerr and let users choose during requests.

items.title: User management
items.text:
Seerr supports multiple user types:

User Type Capabilities Admin Full access, manage settings and users User Request content, view request status Guest Browse only (configurable)

Users can authenticate via:

  • Plex account
  • Jellyfin account
  • Local Seerr account

items.title: Request workflow
items.text:
%%{ init: { "flowchart": { "curve": "basis" } } }%%
flowchart TD
    A([User browses content])
    B([User requests movie/show])
    C[Request approved]
    D[Sent to Radarr/Sonarr]

Requests can be configured for:

  • Auto-approval - Requests are automatically sent to Arr services
  • Manual approval - Admin must approve before processing
  • Request limits - Limit requests per user per time period

items.text:
When embedded service UIs are enabled, Seerr appears in the DUMB frontend with:

  • An embedded UI tab on the Seerr service page
  • A direct link that opens the proxied UI in a new browser tab

This provides a unified interface without exposing Seerr's port directly.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Configure request limits to prevent abuse in multi-user setups.
  • Enable notifications (Discord, email, etc.) to alert users when content is available.
  • Use quality profiles in your Arr services to control download quality.
  • Seerr respects availability settings in Radarr/Sonarr for proper release monitoring.
  • Logs can be viewed via DUMB's Frontend or at /seerr/default/config/logs/jellyseerr.log.

items.title: Sonarr (Core Service)
items.text: Sonarr is a TV series manager that automates monitoring, searching, and organizing episodes through configured indexers and download clients.

items.title: At a glance
items.text:
Test the connections before adding more requests. The saved root folder must also be visible to your media server.

flowchart TD
    A["Open the app from its service page"] --> B
    B["Test indexers and download client"] --> C
    C["Choose the TV root folder and profile"] --> D
    D["Add one intended item and follow import"] --> E
    E["Scan and play it in the media server"]

items.title: First start
items.text:
1. Select Sonarr and its download workflow in DUMB onboarding. Reopen onboarding from Settings → Launch Onboarding if needed.
  2. Open the Sonarr service card. On DUMB Config, use Start if stopped, then select Embedded UI. Complete the application's login setup if prompted.
  3. Open Settings → Download Clients and test the client DUMB created for your selected workflow. Under Settings → Indexers, test an indexer added directly or synced from Prowlarr. Both connections must work to find and acquire media.
  4. Review Settings → Media Management → Root Folders. Choose the curated TV library folder for your workflow and use that same folder in your media server. Review Settings → Profiles to choose the quality you want.
  5. Add one intended series, select that root folder and quality profile, and choose what to monitor. Check Activity → Queue while it is acquired and imported; check Activity → History if it fails.
  6. Scan your media-server library and play the imported item. Finish this test before adding a large library or enabling broad automated searches.

Keep the default SQLite database unless you are planning the separate migration below. The Decypharr, InfiniDysk and AltMount guides explain their different library folders.

items.title: Key configuration fields
items.text:
• core_service: Set to decypharr, infinidysk, altmount, or a list of workflow keys to enable DUMB integration.
  • use_neutarr: Opt this instance into NeutArr automation.
  • use_profilarr: Opt this instance into Profilarr linking.
  • postgres_enabled: Opt this instance into DUMB-managed PostgreSQL config. SQLite is the default; set this to true only when you want Sonarr to use PostgreSQL.
  • postgres_main_db / postgres_log_db: Optional database-name overrides. When blank, DUMB uses sonarr-main and sonarr-log for the default instance, or unique instance-scoped names for additional instances.
  • port: Web UI port (default 8989).
  • pinned_version: Optional version pin for Sonarr updates.
  • repo_owner / repo_name: GitHub repo used for releases or branch builds.
  • release_version_enabled / release_version: Use GitHub releases (e.g., latest, nightly, prerelease, or a tag).
  • clear_on_update: Clear the install directory before updating.
  • exclude_dirs: Directories to preserve when clearing.
  • platforms: Build platforms (defaults to ["dotnet"] when using branches).
  • config_dir, config_file, log_file: Paths for config and logs.

items.title: PostgreSQL database mode
items.text:
SQLite is the default and needs no separate setup. If you want to move an existing Sonarr instance to PostgreSQL, use Database Migration on its service page. Run a rehearsal, review the validation results, then use guarded cutover. Read the migration guide and back up the instance before proceeding.

Geek details: how PostgreSQL settings and startup are generated

When postgres_enabled is true, DUMB:

  • enables the bundled PostgreSQL service if needed;
  • creates the Sonarr main/log databases in postgres.databases;
  • starts PostgreSQL before Sonarr; and
  • writes the required PostgresUser, PostgresPassword, PostgresHost, PostgresPort, PostgresMainDb, and PostgresLogDb entries to Sonarr's config.xml.

During onboarding, enabling postgres_enabled for Sonarr is enough; you do not need to separately select PostgreSQL as an optional service.

This does not migrate existing SQLite data

Setting postgres_enabled: true changes the database backend Sonarr starts with. It does not copy sonarr.db into PostgreSQL.

If you enable this on an existing SQLite-backed Sonarr instance without doing a manual migration, Sonarr can start against fresh PostgreSQL databases and appear empty or newly initialized.

For an existing instance, use the Database Migration tool on its service page. Run a rehearsal first, review its table-count validation, and only then start guarded cutover. See SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration.

Sonarr's upstream documentation still classifies existing SQLite migration as unsupported. Back up Sonarr's /data/sonarr persistence and PostgreSQL's /data/postgres persistence (internal paths /sonarr/... and /postgres_data) before proceeding, even when using DUMB's guarded workflow.

PostgreSQL is not a temporary toggle

There is no known supported migration path from PostgreSQL back to SQLite for Sonarr. Treat postgres_enabled: true as a long-term database choice unless you are willing to recreate the Sonarr instance from scratch.

DUMB preserves the pre-cutover SQLite database and can restore its configuration, but it does not copy later PostgreSQL changes back into SQLite.

items.title: Repo-based installs and updates
items.text:
Sonarr now supports the same repository-based controls as other DUMB services.

  • GitHub releases: Set release_version_enabled: true with a valid repo_owner/repo_name.
  • Default updater: Leave release_version_enabled: false to use the standard Arr updater.

GitHub sources take priority when enabled and are not a fallback. pinned_version only applies to the traditional Arr updater.

  • For AltMount integration, set core_service to altmount and follow the AltMount guide.
  • For combined workflows, set core_service to a list such as ["decypharr", "infinidysk", "altmount"].
  • Use Prowlarr to centrally manage indexers and sync them to Sonarr.
  • DUMB enables Arr folder permission updates and applies permissions to configured root folders during integration.

items.title: Key configuration fields
items.text:
• whisparr_version: Choose v2 or v3 (Eros), or leave blank to detect and preserve the existing version. A new instance with no existing version defaults to v2; review the version-specific guidance below before switching.
  • core_service: Set to decypharr, infinidysk, altmount, or a list of workflow keys to enable DUMB integration.
  • use_neutarr: Opt this instance into NeutArr automation.
  • postgres_enabled: Opt this instance into DUMB-managed PostgreSQL config. SQLite is the default; set this to true only when you want Whisparr to use PostgreSQL.
  • postgres_main_db / postgres_log_db: Optional database-name overrides. When blank, DUMB uses whisparr-main and whisparr-log for the default instance, or unique instance-scoped names for additional instances.
  • port: Web UI port (default 6969).
  • pinned_version: Optional exact numeric release version, such as 3.6.4.1865, within the selected major version. This applies when release_version_enabled is false.
  • repo_owner / repo_name: GitHub release source. Official v2 releases use Whisparr/Whisparr; v3 releases use Whisparr/Whisparr-Eros.
  • release_version_enabled / release_version: Select a GitHub release using latest, prerelease, or an exact tag. When disabled, an unpinned instance still installs the latest official release for its selected version.
  • branch_enabled / branch: Select an update channel: v2 or v2-develop for v2, and eros or eros-develop for v3. These select packaged releases; Whisparr source builds are not supported.
  • commit_sha: Leave blank. Installing Whisparr from a specific source commit is not supported.
  • clear_on_update / exclude_dirs: Generic install-cleanup settings. Whisparr stages a replacement of its managed binary directory; keep config_dir separate from that directory. These fields do not convert databases.
  • config_dir, config_file, log_file: Paths for configuration and logs. Keep different version families in separate data directories.

items.title: Choosing v2 or v3 (Eros)
items.text:
Choose Whisparr v2, Whisparr v3 (Eros), or Detect existing version during onboarding. You can also set whisparr_version on the instance in DUMB Config.

Leaving the setting blank preserves the version indicated by the existing database, installed binary, repository, or update channel. It defaults to v2 only for a new instance without that existing version information.

Version Official release repository Stable / development channel SQLite main database v2 Whisparr/Whisparr v2 / v2-develop whisparr2.db; older installs may use whisparr.db v3 (Eros) Whisparr/Whisparr-Eros eros / eros-develop whisparr3.db

Both versions use logs.db for SQLite logs. DUMB 2.23.0 keeps each instance's binary separate and leaves its configured data directory in place. To use the other version, create a separate instance with its own config_dir and port. DUMB refuses a selected version that conflicts with existing data or a directory containing both families; it does not convert or rename the databases.

Legacy v2 database filenames require a separate migration

Current v2 releases (2.2 and newer) open whisparr2.db; they do not automatically discover or rename a legacy whisparr.db. Starting a newer binary against only the legacy file could create an empty library. See the upstream v2 database path.

DUMB keeps a compatible existing v2 installation working, but blocks an incompatible binary or an update or release pin that would change the expected database filename until you have completed a separately backed-up and validated database migration. It also blocks an older v2 binary against the newer filename and requires deliberate resolution if both filenames or their recovery files are present.

Changing whisparr_version, clearing the install directory, or changing exclude_dirs does not perform this migration. Preserve the original database and recovery files while planning it.

To run both versions at the same time, create a separate instance with its own data directory and port. For example, a separate v3 instance using the official stable releases can use:

{
"whisparr": {
  "instances": {
    "Eros": {
      "enabled": true,
      "whisparr_version": "v3",
      "repo_owner": "Whisparr",
      "repo_name": "Whisparr-Eros",
      "release_version_enabled": true,
      "release_version": "latest",
      "port": 6970,
      "config_dir": "/whisparr/eros",
      "config_file": "/whisparr/eros/config.xml",
      "log_file": "/whisparr/eros/logs/whisparr.txt"
    }
  }
}
}

items.title: PostgreSQL database mode
items.text:
When postgres_enabled is true, DUMB:

  • enables the bundled PostgreSQL service if needed;
  • creates the Whisparr main/log databases in postgres.databases;
  • starts PostgreSQL before Whisparr; and
  • writes the required PostgresUser, PostgresPassword, PostgresHost, PostgresPort, PostgresMainDb, and PostgresLogDb entries to Whisparr's config.xml.

During onboarding, enabling postgres_enabled for Whisparr is enough; you do not need to separately select PostgreSQL as an optional service.

This does not migrate existing SQLite data

Setting postgres_enabled: true changes the database backend Whisparr starts with. It does not copy the existing SQLite database (whisparr2.db, legacy whisparr.db, or whisparr3.db) into PostgreSQL.

If you enable this on an existing SQLite-backed Whisparr instance without doing a manual migration, Whisparr can start against fresh PostgreSQL databases and appear empty or newly initialized.

For an existing instance, use Database Migration on the service page. DUMB requires a rehearsal, initializes an isolated Whisparr-owned PostgreSQL schema, imports and validates every table, and preserves SQLite for rollback. See SQLite to PostgreSQL Migration.

This changes the database backend for the installed Whisparr version. It does not convert a v2 library into a v3 library.

PostgreSQL is not a temporary toggle

There is no known supported migration path from PostgreSQL back to SQLite for Whisparr. Treat postgres_enabled: true as a long-term database choice unless you are willing to recreate the Whisparr instance from scratch.

DUMB can restore the preserved pre-cutover SQLite state, but it does not copy later PostgreSQL writes back into SQLite.

items.title: Repo-based installs and updates
items.text:
DUMB installs ready-to-run official GitHub release archives for the selected Whisparr version. The default install and updater also use these archives; older Servarr nightly and eros download feeds are not used to find current Whisparr releases.

  • Default stable releases: Leave release_version_enabled: false and pinned_version blank.
  • Explicit GitHub release: Set release_version_enabled: true with the matching official repository, then choose latest, prerelease, or a release tag in release_version.
  • Exact numeric pin: Leave release_version_enabled: false and set pinned_version to the exact release version from the selected major version.
  • Development channel: Use v2-develop or eros-develop with branch_enabled: true. Use the corresponding stable channel to stay on stable releases.

An explicit GitHub release selection takes priority over pinned_version. Release tags and pins must match the selected Whisparr major version. Unavailable releases fail the install or update instead of silently switching versions or compiling from source.

Updates replace the managed binary directory after staging the selected release. Configuration and database directories remain separate, and DUMB checks their compatibility before stopping the running service or activating a replacement binary.
